## E0001 TRAINER_BRENDAN_ROUTE_103_MUDKIP class=rival
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: First two useful turns: Pikachu uses Fake Out only on an interruptible threat or Electroweb when the speed drop enables its partner; the starter attacks or sets up only behind a genuinely safe turn. On turn two, exploit the created speed/position advantage rather than repeat Fake Out. Alternate deployment: Pikachu and Shroomish trade immediate starter pressure for disruption and recovery. Reserves & disruption: Taillow is an Orb-activation finisher, not a guaranteed turn-one Guts attacker. Preserve an attack line when sleep is blocked; respect the actual unchosen regional starter. Counterplay & audit: Grass/powder immunity, Electric immunity, priority denial, double targeting, and denying free setup. Disposition: Keep the printed Hoenn seeds; regional generated starter sets require the explicit expansion register, not a false claim that six printed aliases cover all generations.
crack: Grass/powder immunity, Electric immunity, priority denial, double targeting, and denying free setup. Disposition: Keep the printed Hoenn seeds; regional generated starter sets require the explicit expansion register, not a false claim that six printed aliases cover all generations.

## E0002 TRAINER_CALVIN_1 class=regular
strategy: SETUP,TAILWIND
mega_slots: NONE
plan: First two useful turns: Poochyena uses Taunt or Helping Hand according to whether denying setup or securing damage matters more; Zigzagoon drums only when its post-cost HP and legal Gluttony/Figy recovery survive the opposing pair. On the next turn, cash in with Extreme Speed rather than continue setting up. Alternate deployment: Hoothoot Tailwind plus Starly gives an immediate attacking mode without Belly Drum. Reserves & disruption: If Drum is unsafe, attack with Zigzagoon or move to the bird pair. Figy is compatible with Adamant; Unnerve, item suppression or removal can deny recovery. Rattled is an opponent-dependent bonus, not an activation plan. Counterplay & audit: Priority immunity/denial, Fake Out on the support, physical mitigation, berry denial or focused damage before Drum resolves. Disposition: RETAIN; Figy replaces Sitrus to make Gluttony meaningful. Benchmark the first forced route fight against multiple starter pairs, not just a compliant setup fixture.
crack: Priority immunity/denial, Fake Out on the support, physical mitigation, berry denial or focused damage before Drum resolves. Disposition: RETAIN; Figy replaces Sitrus to make Gluttony meaningful. Benchmark the first forced route fight against multiple starter pairs, not just a compliant setup fixture.

## E0003 TRAINER_RICK class=regular
strategy: NONE
mega_slots: NONE
plan: First two useful turns: Scarf Spinarak chooses String Shot when the two-stage Speed drops let Dwebble or Karrablast act usefully before the player; Electroweb offers damaging one-stage control when that is enough. Turn two switches Spinarak when its locked support action no longer produces value. Alternate deployment: Fast control beside Karrablast creates stronger immediate offensive conversion. Reserves & disruption: Dewpider supplies the special Water lane when physical attacks are contained. Do not let a Choice-locked utility move become repeated empty turns. Re-evaluate both targets, turn order, protection, stat-loss immunity, Contrary and retaliatory abilities. Counterplay & audit: Ground immunity blocks Electroweb damage but does not inherently block String Shot. Taunt, Magic Bounce, Clear Amulet, White Herb, speed reversal and punishing switches offer counterplay. Disposition: RETAIN; String Shot replaces Toxic Thread for direct paired speed control, while the Scarf control-and-switch identity remains.
crack: Ground immunity blocks Electroweb damage but does not inherently block String Shot. Taunt, Magic Bounce, Clear Amulet, White Herb, speed reversal and punishing switches offer counterplay. Disposition: RETAIN; String Shot replaces Toxic Thread for direct paired speed control, while the Scarf control-and-switch identity remains.

## E0004 TRAINER_ALLEN class=regular
strategy: PRESSURE
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Sore loser: Allen has never won, and his Pokemon punish anything that weakens them. First two useful turns: Gothita and Pawniard lead. Gothita Fake Outs the foe that threatens Pawniard most, or attacks with Psychic/Thunderbolt when Fake Out has no target worth stopping; Pawniard attacks immediately, choosing Lash Out after its stats were lowered that turn, Sucker Punch to finish a faster attacker, and Iron Head into Fairy types. Alternate deployment: Mankey (Focus Sash) comes in for Rock Slide spread pressure against Flying leads, Close Combat into Normal, Rock, Steel, Ice and Dark targets, and Stomping Tantrum after one of its moves failed. Reserves & disruption: Bunnelby is the fed-up finisher: Huge Power Frustration at friendship zero, Quick Attack to pick off a weakened foe, Rock Slide spread and U-turn to bring a Defiant member back in. Defiant (Pawniard, Mankey) raises Attack by two and Competitive (Gothita) raises Special Attack by two whenever a foe lowers any of their stats, including Intimidate, Electroweb, Icy Wind, Snarl, Bulldoze, Rock Tomb and Fake Tears; credit the boost only when a drop actually happens. Protect when a foe would knock out a member before it acts.
crack: Never lower their stats: no Intimidate, Electroweb, Icy Wind, Snarl or other drops. Use raw damage, burns and paralysis, special attacks into the Defiant pair, Unaware against boosted attackers, Haze or Clear Smog to remove boosts, Fairy and Fire pressure on Pawniard, Fairy, Flying and Psychic pressure on Mankey, and Dark or Ghost pressure on Gothita. Ghosts are immune to Bunnelby's Frustration and Quick Attack. Disposition: user-approved new identity replacing the Light Ball Pikachu and Spore core it shared with the Route 103 rival. Preserve Bunnelby's Huge Power Frustration at friendship zero.

## E0005 TRAINER_TIANA class=casual
strategy: NONE
mega_slots: NONE
plan: First two useful turns: Skitty chooses Fake Out when interruption is necessary, or timely Fake Tears on the same target Swirlix can exploit with special damage; Helping Hand remains the damage-support alternative when defense drops are blocked or less useful. Do not spend a turn lowering Special Defense after the relevant partner attack has already happened. Alternate deployment: Buneary threatens Klutz-assisted Flame Orb Switcheroo while Swirlix attacks. Reserves & disruption: Eevee can receive a Wish on a planned switch or keep itself alive for another attack; Bite is its answer to Ghosts, which Double-Edge cannot touch. An unconsumed Sitrus does not grant Unburden, and switching removes the earned speed bonus. Fake Tears must respect protection, reflection, stat-loss immunity, Contrary, White Herb and retaliatory abilities; it does not help Eevee's physical attacks. Counterplay & audit: Taunt, Magic Bounce, Clear Amulet, status immunity, item protection where supported, and burst damage before Wish resolves. Disposition: RETAIN; Fake Tears replaces Sing to give the whimsical support core a reliable special-damage partnership. No automatic credit for Unburden or guaranteed Orb disruption.
crack: Ghosts block Skitty, Buneary and Double-Edge, leaving Swirlix's Fairy attacks and Eevee's Bite as the answers. Taunt, Magic Bounce, Clear Amulet, status immunity, item protection where supported, and burst damage before Wish resolves. Disposition: RETAIN; Eevee's Bite (user-approved) replaces Quick Attack so two members can hit Ghosts; Fake Tears replaces Sing to give the whimsical support core a reliable special-damage partnership. No automatic credit for Unburden or guaranteed Orb disruption.

## E0006 TRAINER_BILLY class=regular

mega_slots: NONE
plan: First two useful turns: Lotad chooses Rain Dance only when Ducklett's next attack and its own rain turns repay the support action; Ducklett can use Icy Wind or a safe attack while weather is established. Counterplay & audit: Weather replacement, Wide Guard, Grass/Electric pressure, and denying a favorable Ditto target. Disposition: Preserve the rain lesson; attach an ally-damage decision to Surf rather than claiming rain partners are immune.

## E0007 TRAINER_DARIAN class=regular
strategy: SETUP,PRESSURE
mega_slots: NONE
ai: Conservative
plan: First two useful turns: Chinchou's Discharge is a safe ally line beside Ground-type Barboach while Barboach either attacks or uses Dragon Dance behind adequate survival. Turn two evaluates the new speed order before spending another setup turn. Alternate deployment: Tentacool resists neither Ground nor Electric but takes Grass neutrally and threatens Grass attackers with Sludge Bomb. Acid Spray supports an actual special follow-up from Chinchou or Clamperl; value same-turn support only when it lands before the partner attack. Clamperl retains the special Shell Smash mode. Reserves & disruption: Eviolite gives Tentacool working bulk; Liquid Ooze punishes eligible draining attacks, not all Grass damage. Muddy Water attacks both opponents without allied damage. Discharge damages Tentacool and Clamperl: re-evaluate every switch and choose a safer action when warranted. Counterplay & audit: Ground/Electric pressure on Tentacool, Grass pressure on the other three, Taunt, immediate damage and revenge priority. Disposition: Approved Corphish replacement removes the universal Grass weakness while preserving the Chinchou/Barboach engine and marine theme. Shared support forecasts honor order and stat-drop blockers; no forced Acid Spray or Discharge script.
crack: Ground/Electric pressure on Tentacool, Grass pressure on the other three, Taunt, immediate damage and revenge priority. Disposition: Approved Corphish replacement removes the universal Grass weakness while preserving the Chinchou/Barboach engine and marine theme. Shared support forecasts honor order and stat-drop blockers; no forced Acid Spray or Discharge script.

Galarian Yamask has no other authored owner. Dhelmise's first other owner is E0137. Brandi's E0076 Bronzor room is a Psychic/Steel support room, not a Ghost immunity lead. There is no Carvanha/Golbat repeat before Archie's rain crew, and Woods-thug Water Spout is not reused. Preserve the grunt's independent win and the scripted recovery exit before Archie.
crack: Deny the room: Taunt Yamask before its -7 Trick Room, or take it out turn one with two super-effective hits (Dark, Ghost, Grass, Water, Ice), which hands Dhelmise a free attack. Otherwise Protect or switch through the four room turns while Rattata tries to Taunt you out of Protect. Dark, Ghost and Ice hit both leads, and Fire hits Dhelmise. Knock Off strips Yamask's Eviolite, and a Pokemon holding no item blanks Poltergeist. Heavy targets such as Hariyama, Snorlax, Gyarados and Cobalion shrug off Heavy Slam. Fighting hits Rattata four times over and Electric/Grass hits Wailmer, so keep those attackers for the back line instead of wasting them on the Ghost lead.

## E0052 TRAINER_ARCHIE_SLATEPORT class=leader
strategy: RAIN,SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Archie's museum heist crew runs manual rain from a setter that the usual anti-weather tools cannot touch, behind a lead that Psychic attacks cannot touch. Lead: Prankster Sableye, the gem thief Archie brought in for the exhibit hall, beside Archie's own Mightyena. Both are Dark, so Psychic moves do nothing to the lead pair, including an Expanding Force boosted by Psychic Terrain. Turn one: Sableye uses Rain Dance at Prankster priority whenever rain is not up. Damp Rock makes the rain last eight turns, long enough to carry the Swift Swim back line. Sableye is a Ghost, so Fake Out cannot flinch it. It is Dark, so a foe's Prankster Taunt or Encore fails on it. Rain Dance targets the field, so Psychic Terrain does not block it. The rain therefore lands before Aurora Veil, before a Snow Warning user can use its snow, and before any Taunt without priority. Once rain is up, Sableye uses Knock Off on a key item (Choice Specs, Life Orb, Booster Energy, Leftovers, Focus Sash, Eviolite). It uses Prankster Will-O-Wisp on a physical attacker that is not Fire-type, and Prankster Taunt on a Tailwind, Trick Room, Recover, Aurora Veil or terrain user. Under Psychic Terrain its Prankster Taunt and Will-O-Wisp fail against grounded foes and against Dark foes, so it uses Knock Off instead. If a foe's weather replaces the rain while Sableye stands, Sableye sets rain again on the next turn. Mightyena's Intimidate weakens physical attackers on entry. At 113 Speed it moves before unboosted Whimsicott, Indeedee, Ninetales-Alola and Vikavolt at the cap. It uses Throat Chop on a Psychic or Ghost target (it kills Indeedee-M from full), Throat Chop to silence a Bug Buzz or Hyper Voice user, Poison Fang on Grass/Fairy Whimsicott (4x) and on Fairy or Grass targets that resist Dark, Snarl when both foes are special attackers, and Protect on a turn when both foes can hit it super effectively. In rain, Swift Swim Eelektrik (Inclement slot) moves before every unboosted foe. It resists Electric and takes Freeze-Dry neutral. Its Thunder cannot miss in rain, Flash Cannon hits Ninetales-Alola 4x and Fairies 2x, and Giga Drain answers Water Absorb, Storm Drain and Ground types. Lombre is the backup rain dancer: it sets rain again only after snow or sun has overwritten it, never while rain is already up, then attacks with Swift Swim Hydro Pump, Giga Drain or Ice Beam. Corphish uses Dragon Dance only when Sash is intact and no faster foe can KO it through Sash; otherwise it uses Crabhammer, Knock Off or Aqua Jet. Carvanha Protects once to bank Speed Boost, then uses Liquidation, Crunch, or Poison Fang on Fairies. Stats (Hard, cap 30): Sableye 37 is specially bulky (118 HP, 95 SpD), so a cap Life Orb Dazzling Gleam from Indeedee takes about 40% and a cap Modest Floette-Eternal Dazzling Gleam about 55%. Mightyena 36 is 113 Speed and 118 Attack, one point above a cap Timid Whimsicott (112). Eelektrik 36 has 136 Speed EVs, giving 114 Speed in rain. Lombre 35 reaches 144 in rain. Corphish 37 is at 97 Speed after one Dragon Dance. Carvanha 35 reaches 124 after one boost. Could it be cooler? Yes. Mightyena is the wolf Archie led with in the original Emerald and Carvanha grows into his Mega Sharpedo, so the crew is unmistakably his. The museum job brings a gem thief that walks in under Prankster cover and steals items with Knock Off. The rain comes down before anyone else can act, and the eel that loves rain punishes the Electric answer to rain. Overrepresented? Sableye appears elsewhere only as a Will-O-Wisp/Foul Play wall or a Fake Out/Quash supporter, never as a weather setter. The only other Prankster rain setter is the much later Tornadus (E0180). Other Mightyena run Crunch/Play Rough/Sucker Punch attacker kits; this one is Intimidate/Snarl support with Throat Chop and Poison Fang. The nearby museum grunt uses no Dark lead and no rain.
crack: Fairy moves hit both Dark leads super effectively. A Dazzling Gleam or Moonblast from Floette, Whimsicott or Indeedee is the cleanest answer to the lead, and Intimidate does nothing against them. Fighting and Bug moves hit Mightyena and Carvanha. Sableye has only one weakness, but Knock Off and a Specs attack still wear it down, and it has no recovery. Psychic moves no longer touch the lead, so save them for Corphish, Eelektrik and Lombre. To take the weather back, kill Sableye first or bring your weather setter in after the Damp Rock rain runs out; Lombre then has to spend a turn on Rain Dance. A foe's Prankster Tailwind moves before Sableye's Taunt when the foe is faster, and Tailwind cancels the Swift Swim speed edge. Storm Drain or Water Absorb blanks the Water moves of Corphish, Lombre and Carvanha, but not Giga Drain or Thunder. Ground and Grass moves hit Eelektrik, which gives up Levitate for Swift Swim. Electric and Grass moves hit Corphish and Carvanha. Knock Off breaks Corphish's Sash, Encore locks it into Dragon Dance, and Carvanha should be hit before it banks a Speed Boost.

## E0053 TRAINER_GRETA_SLATEPORT class=brain
strategy: ALLY_COMBO
mega_slots: NONE
plan: The Arena Tycoon's exhibition, one Pokemon for each Battle Arena judge plus her Gold-print headliner, and now a lead that no Fake Out can touch. First two useful turns: Umbreon (Mind) and Shedinja (Skill) open together. Umbreon's Inner Focus blocks the flinch and Intimidate, and Fake Out cannot hurt Shedinja at all: it is a Ghost, and Wonder Guard stops a Scrappy Normal hit. Shedinja's Focus Sash means it always gets one action, and its two priority moves act before almost every foe. Shadow Sneak removes a fast Ghost, Psychic or Booster Energy attacker before it moves (at Shedinja's level it one-shots a Booster Energy Flutter Mane even without help). Sucker Punch hits an attacking Steel, Ghost or Psychic. Poltergeist is the 110-power finisher on any foe still holding an item, such as a Mega Charizard, a Sitrus or Life Orb holder or a Focus Sash user. Umbreon uses Helping Hand only on a turn when the boost turns Shedinja's or Gengar's hit into a KO it would otherwise miss, such as Poltergeist into a Mega Charizard Y or Kangaskhan, or Shadow Sneak through Intimidate. Otherwise it uses Snarl against special pairs, Foul Play into a physical attacker, or Thunder Wave on a fast threat that Shedinja cannot reach, so Gengar and Heracross can outspeed it afterwards. Shedinja Protects when two foes that can hit it super-effectively both aim at it. Alternate deployment: when the first lead falls, Gengar (the Gold print) comes in at full HP behind a Focus Sash. A faster Ghost or Dark hit leaves it at 1 HP, and it answers with Sludge Bomb or Shadow Ball on the fast attacker, Thunderbolt on a Charizard or Water/Flying foe (Helping Hand makes that an OHKO on Mega Charizard Y), or Focus Blast on an Incineroar, Kangaskhan or other Dark/Normal/Steel foe. Reserves & disruption: Guts Heracross (Body) comes in last. Its Flame Orb burns it at the end of its first turn, so Intimidate and burns stop mattering, and at Jolly speed it outspeeds Mega Charizard Y. It uses Rock Slide on Flying and Fire pairs, Close Combat on Incineroar, Kangaskhan and Dark/Steel foes, Knock Off on Ghosts (Gholdengo and Flutter Mane included), and Protect when two foes aim at it. Stats: Umbreon is specially bulky support. Shedinja has 1 HP, full Attack and full Speed (Inclement Attack 100), and still moves last without priority. Gengar is a fast special attacker. Heracross is a fast physical attacker. Could it be cooler? The last version led with Gengar, and a Booster Energy Flutter Mane deleted it before it moved. Now the lead is the Arena's precision act: a 1-HP Wonder Guard assassin that Fake Out cannot touch and that strikes first with priority, beside an Inner Focus caddy. The Gold Gengar waits behind it with a Sash, and Heracross waits as the burned bruiser.
crack: Shedinja: Knock Off ignores its Focus Sash. Sand, hail, burn or poison chip ends it. A faster Sucker Punch, Shadow Sneak or Accelerock breaks the Sash before it moves, and Mold Breaker ignores Wonder Guard. Protect the Pokemon it is threatening on turn one, then hit it with any Fire, Flying, Rock, Ghost or Dark attack. Poltergeist fails into a foe with no item (a spent Booster Energy or a Knocked Off item). Umbreon cannot touch Incineroar, takes super-effective Fairy, Fighting and Bug hits, and its Snarl does nothing against physical pairs. Gengar's Sash breaks to Scrappy Fake Out, spread chip or Knock Off, and Incineroar's Knock Off one-shots it. Heracross is unboosted on its first turn, 4x weak to Flying, and 2x weak to Fire, Psychic and Fairy. Flutter Mane's Moonblast and a sun Heat Wave both nearly one-shot it.

## E0069 TRAINER_WALLY_MAUVILLE class=rival
strategy: TAILWIND,ALLY_COMBO
mega_slots: NONE
ai: Conservative
plan: Concept: the rival arc, part zero. Wally still has his childhood team, all four unevolved, but he has watched you win two badges and knows a Steel type walls a Psychic, Fairy, Grass and Normal team. So each partner now carries its own answer to Steel, and the fight tests whether the player brought more than one idea. First two useful turns: Swablu and Roselia lead. Swablu sets Tailwind, or uses priority Helping Hand when the partner's hit is a KO. Roselia is not a free switch-in for Steel. Its Mud Shot does four times damage to Magnezone and double damage to Cobalion, Duraludon and Houndoom, and it lowers the target's Speed. A Helping Hand Mud Shot KOs a full-HP Magnezone. Sleep Powder goes on the biggest awake threat that is not a Grass type, Safeguard side or already asleep. Focus Sash lets Roselia survive one big hit to finish its job. Calm Swablu with Eviolite survives a Thunderbolt or a Stone Edge, then uses Roost to reset. Its Moonblast is a real attack when Taunted, hits Dark and Fighting types super effectively, and can lower Special Attack. Alternate deployment: Kirlia is the ace and enters into Tailwind, so it moves first. Mystical Fire hits Magnezone, Cobalion, Grass, Bug and Ice types super effectively. It also lowers the target's Special Attack every time. Dazzling Gleam is the spread attack for non-Steel pairs, and Psychic covers Fighting and Poison, including Crobat and Hariyama. Protect covers any turn when both foes aim at Kirlia. Trace copies the best opposing ability as Kirlia enters. Flash Fire from Houndoom makes Kirlia immune to Heat Wave. Reserves & disruption: Magneton resists the Steel, Dragon, Fairy and Psychic hits aimed at the rest of the team. Sturdy and Air Balloon mean the first hit only pops the balloon. Volt Switch hands Tailwind turns back to Kirlia or Roselia, and Protect scouts double targets. Never aim Mud Shot at a Flying type, Levitate or an Air Balloon, never aim Mystical Fire into Flash Fire, and never aim Sleep Powder at a Grass type. Could this team be cooler? Yes. The old version won on attempt one with three standing. Every attack it had was Psychic, Fairy, Normal, Grass or Poison, so a lead of Duraludon and Magnezone resisted or ignored all of it. Kirlia wasted turn one on Calm Mind and fell to two Flash Cannons, and Swablu fell to one Analytic Thunderbolt. Now no Steel is safe, the fragile ace arrives only after Tailwind is up, and the lead has a Sash on Roselia and a Calm special-defense set on Swablu. Swablu's Moonblast points toward the Pixilate Mega Altaria of the last rival fight, and Magneton keeps the Air Balloon that its Magnezone carries at Victory Road. Overrepresented? Wally's Roselia is the only Mud Shot Roselia. Daisy's is a Petal Blizzard attacker, and the Victory Road Roselia is a Calm Eviolite sleeper. Sally's Kirlia uses Imprison, not Mystical Fire. Anthony's Magneton is an Analytic Reflect setter, while Wally's is a Sturdy pivot. Levels: cap 30, offsets 5/3/6/2, and Kirlia stays the highest.
crack: Fake Out plus spread Fire on turn one breaks Roselia's Sash and removes it before Mud Shot matters. Taunt Swablu before Tailwind, or set your own Tailwind or Trick Room. Flying types, Levitate and Air Balloon ignore Mud Shot. Water, Fire and Dragon types resist Mystical Fire, and Gyarados takes almost nothing from the team except Magneton's Thunderbolt. Kirlia is still frail: a Dark or Steel hit on the turn it is not Protecting removes the ace. Wide Guard blocks Dazzling Gleam. Grass types and Safeguard stop Sleep Powder. Any hit pops Magneton's Air Balloon. Two hits, or one multi-hit move, break Sturdy, and then Ground does four times damage.

Specs Tinted Lens Mothim provides fast special damage and a U-turn pivot, and is immune to Sandy's Earthquake. Reserves & disruption: Leech Life keeps Araquanid healthy against Grass and Psychic foes. Metal Burst does not use Trash's Attack stat, and an Earthquake beside an unshielded Trash still hits it.
crack: Electric and Flying attacks threaten Araquanid, and Rock attacks threaten Mothim. Once Araquanid is down, Fire attacks again hit Trash for 4x damage and Sandy and Mothim for 2x. Single-target Fire attacks bypass Wide Guard. Taunt, special attacks into Sandy, and giving Trash no hit to return with Metal Burst also work.

## E0092 TRAINER_WATTSON_1 class=leader
strategy: SETUP,ALLY_COMBO
mega_slots: 6
ai: Ace Pokemon
tactic: ACTIVATE ELECTRODE DISCHARGE ELECTIVIRE
plan: Wattson's generator and motor. Leads: Electrode and Electivire. Electrode's Electric Surge lays Electric Terrain on entry, so every grounded Electric attack is 1.3x and nobody grounded can be put to sleep. First two useful turns: Electrode's Discharge hits every other battler on the field, its own partner included, and Electivire's Motor Drive turns that hit into +1 Speed instead of damage; the activation tactic fires it when the board allows and never forces it onto a board where it cannot land. Turn two, the boosted Electivire outruns the player's lead and picks its punch: Wild Charge in the terrain, Ice Punch for the Ground and Flying answers, Cross Chop for the Steel, Normal and Dark ones. Focus Sash Electrode Taunts a Trick Room or setup lead and Volt Switches out to bring a reserve in safely. Reserves: Magnezone floats over Ground on its Air Balloon until the first hit pops it, and Magnet Pull traps Steel types for Thunderbolt and Flash Cannon; Body Press gives it a physical lane. Thundurus is the Prankster: Nasty Plot, Thunderbolt, Grass Knot for the Ground walls Electric cannot touch, and priority Toxic, which poisons those same walls and goes straight through Wonder Guard, so a Shedinja faints at the end of the turn it lands and its Focus Sash never gets to act. Galvantula's Compound Eyes makes Choice Specs Thunder 91% accurate, with Bug Buzz and Energy Ball for the Psychic, Dark and Ground answers. Mega Manectric is the ace: before it Mega Evolves, Lightning Rod draws the player's single-target Electric attacks and absorbs Electrode's Discharge as +1 Special Attack; Mega Evolution trades that for Intimidate, and Flamethrower covers the Steel, Grass, Ice and Bug answers, Shedinja included.
crack: Ground is the obvious answer and it is covered: Ice Punch, Grass Knot, Energy Ball and Toxic all reach it, and Magnezone's balloon keeps it floating until the first hit. The real cracks are Wide Guard or Fake Out on the opening turn to stop the Discharge activation, a Taunt or a faster KO on Electrode, replacing Electric Terrain with another terrain, and physical mitigation such as Intimidate or Reflect against Electivire. Discharge beside Galvantula or Thundurus hurts them, and Mega Evolution ends Manectric's Lightning Rod. A Shedinja now has two answers to dodge: Thundurus's Prankster Toxic, which Dark types, Magic Bounce, Misty Terrain, Safeguard or a Poison or Steel partner turn away, and Mega Manectric's Flamethrower.

## E0094 TRAINER_WILTON_1 class=ace
strategy: TRICK_ROOM
mega_slots: 4
ai: Ace Pokemon
plan: The ruin guardians of northern Route 111, in clear weather. Cofagrigus and Claydol lead, and both carry Trick Room. Fake Out cannot touch the Ghost-type Cofagrigus, and its Mental Herb shrugs off Taunt, so one setter always reaches the move. If a faster foe Imprisons Trick Room first, the seal lasts only while that foe stays in. Claydol's Earth Power and Cofagrigus's Knock Off then focus it. Knock Off ignores Focus Sash in this build and hits the Ghost and Psychic Pokemon that learn Imprison super effectively, and the room goes up the turn after the imprisoner falls. Under the room, Cofagrigus burns the biggest physical threat with Will-O-Wisp, then fires Hex at 130 power into a burned or poisoned target. Its Knock Off strips Sitrus, Leftovers, Sash and Eviolite. Golett (Eviolite, Iron Fist) comes in beside the Levitating Claydol or the armored Mega Steelix, which barely feel it, and uses Earthquake as a spread move. Shadow Punch hits Ghosts, and Thunder Punch answers the Water and Flying Pokemon that three Ground types fear. It does not quake beside Cofagrigus. Mega Steelix (slot 4) uses Body Press off its 230 base Defense and Heavy Slam against light targets, with High Horsepower for Fire and Steel. Claydol, Golett and Steelix keep Protect to scout double targets while the room ticks. Stats: all four have zero Speed IVs and minus-Speed natures. Cofagrigus is Quiet HP/Sp. Atk so Hex is a real threat, and its 145 base Defense still carries Mummy. Claydol is bulky Quiet special, Golett is HP/Attack Brave behind Eviolite, and Steelix is Relaxed HP/Defense for Body Press. Could it be cooler? The sealed tomb opens only for those who break the seal: every piece of the Trick Room plan now has a backup, so the fight turns on outplaying the room, not on one move that switches the whole team off.
crack: Deny or reverse Trick Room. Your own Trick Room cancels it, and a faster Imprison seals it, but Wilton will aim Earth Power and Sash-piercing Knock Off at the imprisoner, so protect it, redirect, or switch it out and back in. Fire and Electric types, Guts and Flash Fire ignore or punish Will-O-Wisp, and without a burn Hex is a modest 65 power. Water attacks hit Claydol, Golett and Mega Steelix super effectively, but Swift Swim works against you under the room, so stall the five turns with Protect and switches, then strike. Knock out Claydol first: Golett then has to stand beside Cofagrigus, where its Earthquake hurts its own partner. Dark and Ghost attacks hit Cofagrigus, Golett and Claydol super effectively, and Grass hits all three Ground types.

Stantler is pure Normal behind Eviolite: Parker keeps it unevolved on purpose, because Wyrdeer would take on the Psychic typing that lets one Dark Pulse delete the room. Reserves & disruption: Wigglytuff is the counter-the-counter - Normal/Fairy with Fur Coat (Inclement slot), it resists the Dark and Bug hits that beat the rest of the room, halves physical damage, opens with Fake Out on entry and answers Dark, Dragon and Ghost leads with Dazzling Gleam and Steel ones with Flamethrower. Instruct only repeats a move the recipient has already used successfully this battle, and Blood Moon cannot be used two turns in a row, so it is not an Instruct target; Earth Power, Hyper Voice and Moonblast are. AI executability: TRICK_ROOM is backed by three setters and the pair planner's own cancellation check; ALLY_COMBO by Telepathy plus the printed INSTRUCT tactics. Every slow member carries a 0 Speed IV and a Speed-lowering or neutral nature; special attackers carry 0 Attack IVs against Foul Play. Could this team be cooler? The old six had four Normal/Psychic members, so one Dark Pulse plus one Dark or Bug hit removed the setter and the guard together on turn 1, and a Spiritomb was immune to almost everything left. Now the Dark lead can only kill one key per turn, the Ghost wall eats a Mind's Eye Blood Moon or a Fairy spread move, and the slowest bear in Hoenn hitting first is the moment to remember - the gym's price theme lives in Blood Moon's every-other-turn limit and the Choice Band lock. Level offsets are individual: Stantler +5 as an Eviolite pre-evolution, Wigglytuff +3 as the frailest body, Bloodmoon Ursaluna +1 because it is already the room's strongest attacker, the rest +2.
crack: Kill both keys on turn 1 or cancel the room. Farigiraf is still Normal/Psychic and falls to one strong Dark or Bug hit, but Stantler only takes super-effective damage from Fighting, so the turn-1 answer is a Dark or Bug nuke into Farigiraf plus a Fighting hit into Stantler - or set your own Trick Room the turn theirs goes up. Armor Tail stops priority only while Farigiraf stands; once it falls, Fake Out and Prankster Taunt work again, and Oranguru's Mental Herb only cures the first Taunt or Encore. Every reset costs Parker a turn at -7 priority, so Protect through the last room turn and punish the re-set. Bloodmoon Ursaluna has no Protect behind its Assault Vest and is weak to Water, Grass, Ice and Fighting; Blood Moon cannot be used two turns running. Lickilicky's Choice Band Earthquake misses Flying and Levitate, and Steel or Poison attacks break Wigglytuff through Fur Coat.

Lucario's Flash Cannon is the faster second Steel hit, and Scrafty is the Psychic-immune body whose Knock Off punishes Psychic attackers; Hariyama's own Knock Off covers Ghosts. Hitmontop is the one member whose job is not to punch hardest: Steadfast turns a flinch into Speed, and Triple Axel's three hits are its Flying answer. Lucario's mixed EV investment is intentional and must not be corrected to a purely physical set. Cadence: two Fake Out users should be spread across turns, not both spent on turn one.
crack: Flying attacks hit three of the four super effectively and Psychic still hits Hitmontop and Hariyama; a fast special Fairy can remove Scrafty and Hitmontop before slow Hariyama Heavy Slams; Ghost types ignore Fake Out and most of the punches; Taunt the guards before the protected turn; special burst beats the physical-heavy dojo; Wide Guard does not stop single-target moves; burn or Intimidate blunts Hariyama's Heavy Slam, and heavy targets shrink it.

Relicanth is 4x weak to Grass, and Runerigus is weak to Grass, Water, Dark, Ghost and Ice. Taunt or Haze stops the Calm Mind endgame.

## E0180 TRAINER_JOSUE class=ace
strategy: RAIN,TAILWIND,MEGA_REVEAL
mega_slots: 2
plan: Josue chases storms across Route 105, and each member is one part of the storm: Pelipper brings the rain, Mega Altaria is the thundercloud, Tornadus is the wind and Kilowattrel is the lightning. First two useful turns: Altaria Mega Evolves on its first turn, so it is already Dragon/Fairy when the first attack lands. It resists Electric and Dark, is immune to Dragon and takes Rock neutrally, and it fires Pixilate Hyper Voice into both foes. Pelipper attacks with rain-boosted Weather Ball or Hurricane, and Focus Sash keeps it alive through the first hit. Once a foe has shown a spread move (Rock Slide, Heat Wave, Discharge, Icy Wind, Blizzard), Pelipper answers with Wide Guard, which covers both members. Wide Guard is a status move, so a Thunderclap aimed at Pelipper that turn fails. Turn two: Hyper Voice again. When Steel or Poison walls Hyper Voice, Altaria uses Ice Beam on a Grass, Ground or Dragon target, or Helping Hand on its partner's attack. Pelipper U-turns out once it can no longer guard. Alternate deployment (the second wave): Tornadus and Kilowattrel. Tornadus's Prankster Tailwind moves first and doubles the side's Speed, and Wind Power charges Kilowattrel on the same turn, so its next Thunder does double damage. If Sand Stream, Drought or Snow Warning has replaced the rain, Tornadus's Prankster Rain Dance takes the weather back before anything else moves, and Damp Rock makes that rain last eight turns. Rain keeps Thunder, Hurricane and Bleakwind Storm at full accuracy. Bleakwind Storm hits both foes and can lower their Speed. Taunt shuts off Trick Room or an opposing weather move. Reserves & disruption: Kilowattrel's Volt Switch can bring Pelipper back, and Drizzle then resets the rain, so the rain can be set three ways: Drizzle on entry, Prankster Rain Dance, and a Volt Switch back into Pelipper. No member's attack touches its partner. Could this team be cooler? The storm concept stays and now covers its own counter: the old all-Flying lineup folded to one Rock Slide under sand, while the thundercloud takes Rock neutrally, shrugs off Electric and Dragon, and hits Tyranitar-style Rock/Dark and Electric/Dragon counters super effectively with a spread move. Offsets stay individual and low: Pelipper +4 as the Sash lead, the rest +3.
crack: Steel is the honest answer. Metagross, Kingambit, Corviknight and similar Steel types wall Hyper Voice, resist Flying, Ice and Fairy, and only have to respect Pelipper's rain Weather Ball and Kilowattrel's Thunder. Electric still does 4x to Pelipper: use Thunderbolt rather than Thunderclap on a Wide Guard turn, and Knock Off removes its Sash first. Poison and Steel hit Mega Altaria super effectively, and Ice hits Altaria, Tornadus and Kilowattrel. Rock Slide still hits the three Flying members before Pelipper has seen a spread move, or once it is gone. Fake Out on Tornadus stops the Tailwind turn. Dark types ignore Prankster Taunt. A second weather setter switched in after Tornadus's one Rain Dance takes the field back for good. Keep Tornadus and Kilowattrel apart, or kill Kilowattrel on the Tailwind turn, and the doubled Thunder never arrives.

Safety Goggles do not stop Lovely Kiss, but Electric or Misty Terrain, Sweet Veil, Insomnia, Vital Spirit and Lum Berry do. Wide Guard blocks Icy Wind. Jynx is frail to Steel, Fire, Rock, Ghost and Dark attacks, and priority finishes Munkidori after its Fake Out turn.

## E0227 TRAINER_MAGIKARP_GUY class=ace
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
ai: Ace Pokemon, Conservative
plan: The Magikarp lover's exam, the one fight the player must enter with six Magikarp, and a floor fight on purpose: an optional Route 118 novelty for a Gyaradosite, not a wall. A player's Magikarp can only ever know Tackle, Flail, Bounce, Facade, Hydro Pump and Splash, so every fish here is a lock that one real Magikarp trick opens - Focus Sash plus Flail, a Flame Orb Facade, Rattled, Eviolite, and two Magikarp hitting one target in the same turn - and nothing carries Grass or Electric, so the player's fish are never simply outclassed. First two useful turns: his own Magikarp and Feebas lead. His Magikarp is the Sash-Flail Magikarp the player dreams of, harmless at full HP and dangerous only from one HP, so it teaches the first rule: two hits in one turn beat any Sash. Feebas is the Sash-breaker: Eviolite, Timid speed and an Icy Wind that chips both player leads off full HP, so a Sash Magikarp led into it is spent before it Flails and both leads are slowed under the ace; Tickle softens the next hit and Mirror Coat only punishes a Hydro Pump. It is paper-thin physically, so two Tackles or one Facade take most of it. Alternate deployment: Wishiwashi comes in schooled and heavy-hitting behind a Life Orb, with Beat Up to shred any Focus Sash in one multi-hit move and Liquidation for real damage, but it has no Def investment, no Leftovers and no Protect, and the Life Orb eats its own HP toward the 25 per cent line where the school scatters; two Facades a turn for two turns break it, and a lone Wishiwashi can only Endeavor, which drags a Magikarp straight into Flail range. Pyukumuku is the patience lock: Counter doubles any hit back, Innards Out hits whoever finishes it, Toxic poisons and Venom Drench then cuts a poisoned Magikarp's Attack and Speed, and Helping Hand powers the ace. Reserves & disruption: Gyarados, one level up, is the ace and the promise of what the player's Magikarp become. Intimidate lowers Magikarp Attack but triggers Rattled, and its Black Glasses Crunch is its best hit into Water fish - also a Dark hit that gives a Rattled Magikarp another Speed stage; Dragon Dance and a Helping Hand from Pyukumuku or Wishiwashi are the only way it one-shots an ordinary Magikarp. Bounce is the move the player's own Magikarp know, shown at full strength. Every fish sits at the cap and Gyarados one above: this is an exam of Magikarp tricks, not a stat check.
crack: Lead Flame Orb Facade Magikarp, not Sash ones - Feebas's Icy Wind breaks any Sash on turn one. Put two hits into his Magikarp in one turn so its Sash cannot save it, and Facade Feebas before its Icy Winds pile up. Double Facade Wishiwashi two turns running to scatter the school; its Life Orb helps you. Leave Pyukumuku for last and bring Flame Orbs, not Toxic Orbs, so Venom Drench has nothing to cut; finish it with a Magikarp that is already at one HP, which loses nothing to Counter or Innards Out. Save a Jolly Rattled Sash Magikarp and an Eviolite Magikarp for Gyarados: Intimidate makes the Rattled one faster than a Dragon Danced Gyarados, the Eviolite one takes two Crunches, the Sash one answers from one HP with a 200-power Flail, and switching a Magikarp out resets the Intimidate drop.

## E0243 TRAINER_GRUNT_WEATHER_INST_1 class=grunt
strategy: TAILWIND
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Raid stage 1 - the lobby, the boarding party that came through the door before anyone reached the machines, so this is the one room in the Institute with no weather at all: the crew brings its own wind instead. First two useful turns: Crobat opens with Tailwind, and Inner Focus means no Fake Out and no Intimidate can stop it. Tailwind lands before a fast player lead moves, and turn order updates within the turn, so Crawdaunt's Adaptability Knock Off or Crabhammer hits on turn one ahead of a fast Electric attacker. Crawdaunt wears a Covert Cloak, so a Fake Out chips it but cannot flinch it; the boarding strike cannot be stalled with Fake Out. Knock Off punishes a Ghost/Steel pivot hard, and Crabhammer does the same to a Rock/Dark one. Turn two runs under Tailwind: Brave Bird removes a Grass lead, and Quick Guard is Crobat's answer when the player's plan is priority (Grassy Glide, Fake Out, Sucker Punch), because Tailwind cannot outrun priority. Crawdaunt Protects when both foes can threaten it. Alternate deployment: Whiscash is the anchor behind them. It is immune to Electric, and Oblivious ignores Intimidate and Taunt. Under Tailwind its Rock Slide goes first with a flinch chance against a Flying Electric lead, High Horsepower is single-target (so it never hits an ally, and Grassy Terrain does not halve it) and hits Steel, Rock and Fire pivots, and Helping Hand turns Crawdaunt's next hit into a knockout. A Rindo Berry lets it take one priority Grass hit. Reserves & disruption: Tentacruel is the black flag. Liquid Ooze punishes every drain move, Acid Spray drops Special Defense by two stages ahead of Muddy Water or Sludge Bomb, and Icy Wind is the crew's second speed control for the turns after Tailwind expires. It is also Super Effective on a Flying Electric attacker. AI executability: TAILWIND has a real, flinch-proof setter, and the planner models this turn's order change, so it can plan the Crawdaunt hit behind it. Quick Guard, Protect and Helping Hand are all planner-scored. Could this team be cooler? Yes, and this version is. The old lobby lost to one fast Electric attacker: Golbat, Crawdaunt and Tentacruel were all weak to Electric, Crawdaunt died before acting in every benchmark run, and Liepard's Prankster Encore and Taunt did nothing against Dark types or Good as Gold. Now the crew raises its sails (Tailwind), boards in a cloak (Covert Cloak Crawdaunt), keeps an anchor the lightning cannot touch (Whiscash) and flies the black flag (Tentacruel). The moment to remember is a player's Fake Out bouncing off a cloaked Crawdaunt while its Knock Off lands before their Electric attacker moves. Honest counterplay: priority ignores Tailwind, Crobat has no Protect, and the wind lasts four turns. Level offsets are individual: Crawdaunt +5 as the strike, Crobat, Whiscash and Tentacruel +4.
crack: Priority is the key. Tailwind does not outrun Grassy Glide, Sucker Punch or Aqua Jet, and a Grassy Glide still KOs Crawdaunt through the cloak, so pair priority with a second attacker to force Crobat's Quick Guard or Crawdaunt's Protect. Crobat has no Protect: a fast Rock, Ice or Electric hit removes it, and Tailwind can't be set again. Protect or switch through the four Tailwind turns, or answer with your own Tailwind or Trick Room. Whiscash is Grass-weak 4x behind a single Rindo Berry, three of the four still fear special Electric once the wind drops, and no drain move is safe while Tentacruel's Liquid Ooze is on the field.

Frosmoth is 4x weak to Fire and Rock - a single-target Stone Edge or two Fire hits get through Occa Berry and Wide Guard. Keep Grassy Glide or other priority for Sharpedo's switch-in turn, before Speed Boost pays out.

## E0248 TRAINER_SHELLY_WEATHER_INSTITUTE class=admin

Alternate deployment: Castform beside Ninetales is the Institute's own research Pokemon turned against its keepers - under Shelly's snow Forecast makes Castform an Ice type, so Weather Ball is a 100-power same-type attack and Blizzard never misses; it is the thematic heart of the fight. Reserves & disruption: Rotom-Wash is the Levitate Electric pivot, and Clefable's Unaware means a player who answered the grunts by setting up finds those boosts simply ignored. AI executability: SNOW has an automatic setter, REDIRECTION a real Follow Me user, SETUP a real Dragon Dance; the custom Mega Feraligatr transition remains a source and native gate to confirm. Could this team be cooler? Yes, and one slot was quietly dead: Kingdra's Damp does nothing outside Explosion and Aftermath, so the boss was carrying a 540-BST body with a blank ability and a generic special kit. Castform replaces it with the one Pokemon that belongs in this building more than any other, and its ability is not flavour - Forecast is the mechanic that ties the boss to the room she is standing in. Clefable is likewise re-read as the Institute's own, which resolves the only other thematic loose end. The moment to remember is a Castform turning white as Shelly's snow lands and immediately throwing a perfect-accuracy Blizzard. Honest counterplay: take the weather back and four of her six get worse at once. Level offsets are individual and boss-grade: Castform +5 because it is a frail 420-BST body carrying a key role, Mega Feraligatr +3, the support core +3 to +4.
crack: Replace the snow. Drought, Drizzle or Sand Stream simultaneously ends Aurora Veil's reason for existing, Castform's typing and Blizzard's accuracy. Failing that, remove screens with Brick Break or Defog, attack Clefable rather than routing around Follow Me, bring Grass and Electric for the Water core, and keep your own stat boosts off the table while Unaware and Competitive are on the field.

## E0249 TRAINER_BRENDAN_ROUTE_119_MUDKIP class=rival
strategy: TAILWIND,REDIRECTION
mega_slots: NONE
ai: Ace Pokemon
plan: Rival concept - the rival read the Route 119 forecast and built for the storm instead of against it. This map rains for the whole battle, so every rain trick on this team is free and permanent: Thunder cannot miss, Scald hits half again as hard, and Fire aimed at the rival's Grass and Ice-weak members is halved. All six branch aliases share slots 1 to 5; only the regional starter ace in slot 6 changes by branch. First two useful turns: Manectric and Milotic lead, and neither needs a free turn, so Fake Out plus a spread move no longer decides the fight. Manectric's Focus Sash keeps it alive to act: Thunder into Flying and Water targets (Tornadus, Gyarados, Swift Swim attackers), Snarl against two special attackers, or Volt Switch out ahead of a slower Ground attacker, ideally into Swellow, which is immune to Earthquake and whose Flame Orb then activates at the end of that same turn. Lightning Rod pulls every single-target Electric attack away from Milotic. Milotic is the Feebas the rival fished from under the Route 119 bridge: Competitive turns an Intimidate, Parting Shot or Snarl into +2 Special Attack; Icy Wind slows both foes and is four times effective on Garchomp and super effective on Tornadus and Grass attackers; Ice Beam removes Garchomp; rain Scald burns the physical counters; and a Rindo Berry halves the first Grass hit aimed at it. Protect covers it from a double target. Alternate deployment: Swellow is the back-line cleaner, not the lead. It enters on a Volt Switch or after a faint, takes its burn at the end of that turn, then hits with 140-power Guts Facade or Brave Bird; Tailwind is its play only when the player's side has the speed order. Weavile enters with Fake Out and priority Ice Shard: with Life Orb, Ice Shard removes an undamaged Garchomp and finishes a Tornadus or Grass attacker that Icy Wind or Ice Beam has chipped, and Triple Axel and Knock Off (Goggles, Assault Vest, Eviolite, Sitrus) cover the rest. Reserves & disruption: Breloom's Spore and Mach Punch punish anything without Grass typing or Goggles, and Rock Slide gives it an answer to the rain birds. Ace: Sceptile, the rival's own Treecko, with the Inclement Chloroplast ability - its sunlight moves work in any weather, so in the storm Solar Beam fires in one turn at full power (120-power Grass STAB with Life Orb; four times effective on Mega Swampert and Gastrodon) and Synthesis restores two thirds. Earth Power covers the Fire, Steel and Poison types that resist Grass, and Protect scouts a double target. In another starter generation the runtime swaps in that generation's Grass starter with its native set. AI executability: TAILWIND is backed by Swellow and only scores when it buys speed-order crossings; REDIRECTION is backed by Lightning Rod. No RAIN flag: the rain belongs to the map and the team never sets it. Could this be cooler? The old leads were two frail members that one Fake Out plus Rock Slide removed, and its storm plan was two redirection abilities a smart player simply never fed; now the rival's three signatures (Guts Swellow, Poison Heal Breloom, Lightning Rod Manectric) sit behind a lead that acts through Fake Out, the Route 119 Feebas punishes the Intimidate lead that used to start the fold, and the ace is a Sceptile that photosynthesises in the rain.
crack: The storm is the rival's engine, so either take it away or play around what it powers. Your own sun, sand or snow setter makes Thunder miss and weakens Scald, though Chloroplast keeps Sceptile's Solar Beam instant in any weather. Do not lead Intimidate, Parting Shot or Snarl into Milotic: Competitive turns each into +2 Special Attack. Milotic falls to Grass and Electric, but Lightning Rod takes single-target Electric while Manectric is out and the Rindo Berry halves the first Grass hit, so plan two Grass hits, a spread Electric move, or remove Manectric first. Manectric's Sash breaks to Fake Out or any chip, and then one Ground attack removes it; its Volt Switch usually brings in Swellow, so a Rock Slide or Electric attack aimed at that slot punishes the pivot. Swellow is frail and Rock-weak, Breloom is four times weak to Flying, and Safety Goggles or a Grass type blanks Spore. Weavile is four times weak to Fighting and loses health to Life Orb on every hit, so Mach Punch, Close Combat or a Rock Slide removes it; its own Fake Out works only on the turn it enters. Sceptile's coverage is Grass plus Ground, so a Flying type (Tornadus, Corviknight) walls it, and Ice, Flying, Bug and priority hurt it; Synthesis heals two thirds a turn in the storm, so finish it in one turn rather than chipping it.
MANECTRIC @FOCUS_SASH LIGHTNING_ROD TIMID 4/0/0/252/0/252 4 | THUNDER, VOLT_SWITCH, SNARL, PROTECT | ivs=31/0/31/31/31/31 | friendship=255
MILOTIC @RINDO_BERRY COMPETITIVE MODEST 252/0/4/252/0/0 5 | SCALD, ICE_BEAM, ICY_WIND, PROTECT | ivs=31/0/31/31/31/31 | friendship=255
SWELLOW @FLAME_ORB GUTS JOLLY 4/252/0/0/0/252 4 | FACADE, BRAVE_BIRD, TAILWIND, PROTECT | ivs=31/31/31/31/31/31 | friendship=255
BRELOOM @TOXIC_ORB POISON_HEAL JOLLY 4/252/0/0/0/252 5 | SPORE, MACH_PUNCH, SEED_BOMB, ROCK_SLIDE | ivs=31/31/31/31/31/31 | friendship=255
WEAVILE @LIFE_ORB PICKPOCKET JOLLY 4/252/0/0/0/252 4 | FAKE_OUT, ICE_SHARD, TRIPLE_AXEL, KNOCK_OFF | ivs=31/31/31/31/31/31 | friendship=255
SCEPTILE @LIFE_ORB CHLOROPLAST TIMID 4/0/0/252/0/252 6 | SOLAR_BEAM, EARTH_POWER, SYNTHESIS, PROTECT | ivs=31/0/31/31/31/31 | friendship=255

Ace: Sceptile, the rival's own Treecko, with the Inclement Chloroplast ability - its sunlight moves work in any weather, so in the storm Solar Beam fires in one turn at full power (120-power Grass STAB with Life Orb; four times effective on Mega Swampert and Gastrodon) and Synthesis restores two thirds. Earth Power covers the Fire, Steel and Poison types that resist Grass, and Protect scouts a double target. In another starter generation the runtime swaps in that generation's Grass starter with its native set. AI executability: TAILWIND is backed by Swellow and only scores when it buys speed-order crossings; REDIRECTION is backed by Lightning Rod. No RAIN flag: the rain belongs to the map and the team never sets it. Could this be cooler? The old leads were two frail members that one Fake Out plus Rock Slide removed, and its storm plan was two redirection abilities a smart player simply never fed; now the rival's three signatures (Guts Swellow, Poison Heal Breloom, Lightning Rod Manectric) sit behind a lead that acts through Fake Out, the Route 119 Feebas punishes the Intimidate lead that used to start the fold, and the ace is a Sceptile that photosynthesises in the rain.
crack: The storm is the rival's engine, so either take it away or play around what it powers. Your own sun, sand or snow setter makes Thunder miss and weakens Scald, though Chloroplast keeps Sceptile's Solar Beam instant in any weather. Do not lead Intimidate, Parting Shot or Snarl into Milotic: Competitive turns each into +2 Special Attack. Milotic falls to Grass and Electric, but Lightning Rod takes single-target Electric while Manectric is out and the Rindo Berry halves the first Grass hit, so plan two Grass hits, a spread Electric move, or remove Manectric first. Manectric's Sash breaks to Fake Out or any chip, and then one Ground attack removes it; its Volt Switch usually brings in Swellow, so a Rock Slide or Electric attack aimed at that slot punishes the pivot. Swellow is frail and Rock-weak, Breloom is four times weak to Flying, and Safety Goggles or a Grass type blanks Spore. Weavile is four times weak to Fighting and loses health to Life Orb on every hit, so Mach Punch, Close Combat or a Rock Slide removes it; its own Fake Out works only on the turn it enters. Sceptile's coverage is Grass plus Ground, so a Flying type (Tornadus, Corviknight) walls it, and Ice, Flying, Bug and priority hurt it; Synthesis heals two thirds a turn in the storm, so finish it in one turn rather than chipping it.

## E0251 TRAINER_HIDEO class=ace
strategy: MEGA_REVEAL
mega_slots: 4
plan: Concept - a ninja clan in the Route 119 jungle grass: two fast shadows up front that Earthquake cannot touch, a smoke bomb behind them, and Mega Gengar's cage to finish. First two useful turns: Crobat and Greninja lead, and neither is weak to Ground (Crobat is immune, Greninja neutral). Crobat's Inner Focus makes Fake Out and Intimidate slide off; it outspeeds and Taunts the Tailwind or Trick Room setter, or raises Quick Guard when the side faces Fake Out, Sucker Punch, Thunderclap, Extreme Speed or a Prankster move, and Super Fang halves the bulky wall Greninja cannot dent. Greninja's first attack fixes its Protean type for the entry: Ice Beam deletes a Ground or Dragon lead such as Mega Garchomp, priority Water Shuriken (boosted on Route 119's rainy days) breaks Focus Sash and Disguise and picks off anything low, and Dark Pulse answers Ghosts and Gholdengo. Alternate deployment: when a lead falls, Salazzle arrives with Fake Out, then throws Poison Gas, a spread smoke bomb that Corrosion lets poison Steel and Poison types too; Heat Wave burns through the Steels and Sludge Bomb covers Fairies. Reserves: Mega Gengar evolves the turn it lands (MEGA_REVEAL) so Shadow Tag traps both foes at once, then Hex hits at 130 power on every poisoned target while Icy Wind keeps the speed race. Sludge Bomb's own poison chance feeds Hex when Poison Gas missed or never came. The fight is a sequence: poison the board, lock it, and Hex it down. Could this team be cooler? The old poison squad was four Ground weaknesses in a row and Muk never did anything but Helping Hand; this version keeps Salazzle and Mega Gengar, finally gives Corrosion something to corrode, and puts the literal ninja Pokemon and a Quick Guard shadow in front. The moment to remember is Water Shuriken finishing a sashed foe before it moves, and Shadow Tag closing the door on a poisoned board. Offsets individual: Mega Gengar +2 as the ace.
crack: Electric and Rock spread moves (Discharge, Electroweb, Rock Slide) hit both leads super-effectively; Crobat's Wacan Berry softens only the first Electric hit, and Crobat has no Protect. Protect your Ground or Dragon on turn one instead of attacking into Ice Beam; once Greninja's Protean has locked a type (often pure Ice after Ice Beam), punish that type with Rock, Fighting, Fire or Steel. Good as Gold, Misty Terrain, a Lum Berry or a status of your own blanks Poison Gas and turns Hex back into a 65-power move, and Taunt stops the smoke bomb outright. Ghost types ignore Shadow Tag but take super-effective Hex and Dark Pulse, so pick a bulky one. Save Earthquake for the back line: Salazzle is 4x weak (chip it before the Sash matters) and Mega Gengar is 2x weak.

Flamigo's U-turn pivots it out when the board turns to Electric or Flying attackers, so a fresh archer or Toucannon takes the slot. Hisuian Decidueye is the room's answer to the Electric and Rock spread every Fortree challenger brings: Grass/Fighting resists both, and its Yache Berry halves the first Ice hit. On turn two whichever archer still stands keeps attacking, and Protect is only for a visible double target. Alternate deployment: Sirfetch'd and Toucannon are the bulky second wave. Sirfetch'd carries an Assault Vest against special Electric and Ice attackers, Knock Off for Ghost and Psychic types and Poison Jab for Fairy types. Toucannon's Skill Link Rock Blast and Bullet Seed always hit five times, which breaks Focus Sash and Substitute. Rock Blast is for Weavile, Zapdos and the other Ice or Flying answers, and Bullet Seed is for Tyranitar and Water types. Reserves & disruption: Bombirdier's Rocky Payload Rock Slide is the spread answer to the opposing birds and Fire types that challengers bring to a bird gym, and its Rocky Helmet punishes Fake Out and other contact. AI executability: PRESSURE - the archers trade HP for damage instead of stalling, and nothing claims a setup, weather or Tailwind the room does not have. Could this team be cooler? The old room was a setup room (Quiver Dance, Swords Dance, Prankster Tailwind) that never got a setup turn, behind five birds that were each weak to Rock and Electric. Now its threat is what it hits, not what it sets up: the Fighting moves land on the exact team a player brings to a bird gym, and Intimidate does not slow the hunters. Asked again, Scrappy is the cooler touch: the Intimidate lead does nothing to the archers, and Gholdengo, the usual Ghost-type wall for Fighting moves, is no longer safe from Close Combat. Offsets: kept species keep their earlier offsets (Hisuian Decidueye and Noctowl +2, Bombirdier +3, Toucannon +4 from Edwardo's room). New Flamigo and Sirfetch'd are +3.

Fairy and Psychic attacks hit all three fighters super-effectively. Fake Out the faster archer and Protect the target of the other. Flamigo's Life Orb and Brave Bird recoil wear it down, Assault Vest Sirfetch'd cannot Protect, and Sucker Punch fails into a status move.

strategy: NONE
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Room concept - the scavengers. Edwardo's flock bleeds the attacker weak first, and then the hunters finish it. When Jumpluff is about to fall, Memento lowers a foe's Attack and Special Attack by two stages each, so the next bird comes in against a crippled foe. Reserves & disruption: the finishers come in once the foes are weakened. Moxie Honchkrow's Sucker Punch and Brave Bird snowball off every knockout. Choice Band Reckless Staraptor's Brave Bird and Close Combat hit hardest of all, and Close Combat hits Mega Tyranitar, Kingambit and Weavile for four times damage. AI executability: no weather, Trick Room or Tailwind is claimed. The drops are ordinary status moves, and Strength Sap is chosen as recovery. The old carrion room stood on a Focus Sash Jumpluff's Rage Powder and Sleep Powder, which Taylor's Vivillon already does on Route 119. One Fake Out and Mega Tyranitar's sand ended it, and Honchkrow's Moxie never started. Now Jumpluff heals from the very Attack it drains, and a player's Rock Slide lands after two or three Attack drops instead of at full power. Asked again, Memento is the scavenger's bargain: the bird that is going down anyway takes two stages off the threat on its way out. Offsets: kept species keep their earlier offsets (Jumpluff +5, Mandibuzz and Honchkrow +4, Togekiss +2 from Darius's room). New Squawkabilly is +6 as the frail Intimidate pivot, and new Staraptor is +3.
crack: The drops are the whole plan, so bring Pokemon that ignore them or punish them. Defiant Kingambit gains Attack from Squawkabilly's Intimidate. Special attackers are only touched by Parting Shot and Memento, so Specs Magnezone, Raging Bolt and Iron Bundle remove the Electric- and Ice-weak flock, and Jumpluff is four times weak to Ice. Switching out resets every drop. Taunt shuts Jumpluff and Mandibuzz down, Sucker Punch fails into a status move, and Choice Band Staraptor is locked and pays heavy recoil.

## E0286 TRAINER_ASHLEY class=gym
strategy: RAIN,SETUP,TAILWIND
mega_slots: 6
plan: Room concept - the storm room, and the only one in Fortree where the sky is wet. First two useful turns: Pelipper's Drizzle lands on entry and it chooses between Tailwind and immediate Hurricane/Muddy Water pressure - under its own rain Hurricane never misses, which is the reason this room exists. Gyarados leads beside it, drops Intimidate on both player slots and either attacks or takes one Dragon Dance behind Lum Berry; its Earthquake is a free spread move because every partner flies. The room's Electric answer is Emolga, the storm's own lightning. Motor Drive makes it immune to Electric moves and turns every one aimed at it into +1 Speed, so the Electric sweeper every Fortree challenger brings cannot touch it. Its job is to disarm that sweeper: Eerie Impulse cuts the Electric attacker's Special Attack by two stages, halving the spread Electric damage the four-times-weak flock would take, and Encore locks a terrain setter, Protect or setup move into repeating itself. Focus Sash guarantees it that action against the non-Electric hit. Under the rain Thunder never misses, so Emolga's own STAB punishes the Water and Flying types the player brings. Turn two converts: Mantine's Swift Swim comes online, Swanna's Hydration scrubs any status at end of turn and its Weather Ball is a 100-power Water move. Alternate deployment: Pelipper and Mantine are the bulky special rain pair when the player's lead punishes physical setup. Reserves & disruption: Mega Pidgeot's No Guard-grade Hurricane accuracy is redundant in rain but its Heat Wave is actively weakened by it - the AI must not pick the Fire option under its own weather. AI executability: RAIN has an automatic setter, TAILWIND a real user, SETUP a genuine Dragon Dance. Could this team be cooler? Yes. Five of six members took four-times Electric damage and one Earthquake on Gyarados was not enough to stop a terrain sweep. Cramorant goes: its Surf was the one move that hit partners, and it was another four-times Electric weakness. Emolga keeps the room a flock of storm birds and answers lightning with lightning rather than borrowing a ground-bound counter.
crack: Remove Emolga before it acts - it is frail once the Sash is broken, so a multi-hit or chip-then-hit works, and Ice or Rock hits it super-effectively - then Electric pressure works again. Physical Electric attackers ignore Eerie Impulse; switching resets it and Encore. Drought or Sand Stream removes Hurricane and Thunder accuracy, Mantine's Speed and Swanna's Weather Ball in one turn; Rock handles Pelipper and Pidgeot; Gyarados folds to a single Electric move if it spends its first turn on Dragon Dance instead of Earthquake.

## E0287 TRAINER_HUMBERTO class=gym
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Room concept - six flyers that refuse to pay the usual price. A bird normally pays for the Rock Slide, the Thunderbolt, the sand, its own Life Orb and the player's screens. In Humberto's room each of those prices is refused or billed back. Sigilyph sets Reflect and Light Screen from Light Clay (eight turns), so every Rock Slide, Ice Shard or Thunderbolt does about a third less in a double battle, and Magic Guard means sand never chips it. Dragonite's Multiscale halves the first hit it takes at full HP, and its Weakness Policy turns the first super-effective hit (Rock Slide, Ice Shard, Icy Wind) into +2 Attack and Special Attack, so the obvious attack makes it stronger. Gliscor is Ground/Flying, so Electric moves cannot touch it, and Poison Heal turns its own Toxic Orb into 12.5% recovery every turn. Hawlucha's Limber blocks paralysis from Thunder Wave, Nuzzle and a Static Zapdos. Crobat's Infiltrator ignores the player's Reflect, Light Screen, Aurora Veil and Substitute. Unaware Swoobat ignores the player's stat boosts, a Defiant Kingambit's included. First two useful turns: Sigilyph and Dragonite lead. On turn one Sigilyph sets Reflect, or Light Screen when both foes are special, while Dragonite attacks or Protects from a visible double target. A player who Rock Slides or Ice Shards into the pair triggers Weakness Policy. On turn two Sigilyph sets the other screen and Dragonite attacks: +2 Extreme Speed goes first, Dragon Claw is for Dragons, and Fire Punch is for Steel and Ice types. Alternate deployment: Gliscor is the Electric answer. High Horsepower hits Magnezone for four times and Tyranitar, Kingambit, Incineroar, Iron Hands, Raging Bolt and Gholdengo for double. Knock Off removes items and goes through Focus Sash, and Taunt stops a Trick Room, Tailwind or screen setter. Reserves & disruption: Hawlucha takes a Swords Dance behind screens and uses Close Combat on the Rock, Dark and Steel answers. Crobat is the fastest member: its Brave Bird and Cross Poison ignore a Substitute or an Aurora Veil, Cross Poison covers Fairy types, and U-turn pivots it out to bring a fresh member in. Swoobat's Calm Mind and Psychic make it the late cleaner, and a boosted foe cannot outscale it. AI executability: SETUP is backed by Hawlucha's Swords Dance and Swoobat's Calm Mind. The screens are ordinary support, and nothing claims weather, Trick Room or Tailwind. Could this team be cooler? The old room had the right idea, but four of its six refusals were copies: Jennifer's Mirror Armor, Colin's Magic Bounce, the Motor Drive of Jackson's Rotom and Ashley's Emolga, and Carolina's White Herb Unburden. Its Gliscor and Corviknight lead also folded to one Weavile and one Zapdos. The new lead makes those two moves cost the player: Ice Shard into Dragonite is billed back as +2, Thunderbolt does nothing to Gliscor, and both land under screens. Asked again, Crobat's Infiltrator is the twist: the room's own screens stay up, while Crobat's attacks pass straight through the player's. Offsets: kept species keep their earlier offsets (Sigilyph, Gliscor and Hawlucha +2, Dragonite +1 from Flint's room). New Crobat is +2 and Swoobat +4 as the frailest member.
crack: Every refusal has its own price. Knock Off or a neutral hit removes Weakness Policy before anything super-effective lands. Brick Break, Psychic Fangs or Raging Bull shatter the screens, or you can stall out the eight turns. Ice is four times effective on both Gliscor and Dragonite, and Water also removes Gliscor. Knock Off the Toxic Orb before its first end of turn, or simply out-damage Poison Heal. Sigilyph, Crobat, Hawlucha and Swoobat are frail: Electric and Ice still hit all four super-effectively, Rock hits all but Hawlucha, and Dark attacks hit Sigilyph and Swoobat for double. Fake Out on Sigilyph delays the screens a turn.

Mega Aerodactyl is the ace and Mega Evolves on its first turn. AI executability: TAILWIND has two setters, and the Steel one survives Rock Slide. Keep Icy Wind, Electroweb and Intimidate away from Braviary, and use plain damage instead. Rock Slide still hits everything except Corviknight for double, and Yanmega for four times. Protecting through the four Tailwind turns takes Darius's speed edge away from everything except Yanmega and Mega Aerodactyl.

## E0289 TRAINER_WINONA_1 class=leader
strategy: SETUP,TAILWIND
mega_slots: 6
ai: Ace Pokemon
plan: Leader concept - the whole sky, and nothing on the ground can reach it. All six of Winona's Pokemon are airborne, and she decides the speed of turn one herself. Lead: Gale Wings Talonflame with Covert Cloak, beside Contrary Enamorus. At full HP, Talonflame's Tailwind is a Flying move with priority. Covert Cloak means Fake Out cannot flinch Talonflame, so Tailwind goes up on turn one ahead of every normal-priority move. Even if a Fake Out chips Talonflame and Gale Wings is lost, Jolly Talonflame still outspeeds the field and sets Tailwind that turn. Tailwind doubles Speed immediately, so Enamorus attacks the same turn, ahead of Iron Bundle, Mega Raichu or Weavile. Superpower is a one-hit KO on Ice, Steel, Dark and Rock leads. Play Rough is a one-hit KO on Mega Raichu and on Fighting and Dragon leads. Earth Power hits Fire and Electric. Under Contrary, every Superpower raises Enamorus's Attack and Defense, and an Intimidate or Parting Shot gives it a free boost. Yache Berry halves the first Ice hit, so a Specs Freeze-Dry or Ice Shard can no longer remove Enamorus for free. While it is untouched, Talonflame fires priority Brave Bird; Flare Blitz covers Steel, Grass and Ice. Once a foe has shown a priority move, Talonflame raises Quick Guard, which blanks the Fake Out, Ice Shard, Grassy Glide, Sucker Punch and Extreme Speed aimed at the pair. Back line: Celesteela invests in Speed so that it moves first under Tailwind. Earthquake is a free spread move because nobody on Winona's side touches the ground; it is aimed at Electric, Fire, Rock and Steel foes. Rock Slide punishes the Electric, Fire and Ice foes that hunt flyers. Heavy Slam, from a 999.9 kg body, hits Fairy, Ice and Rock. Wide Guard goes up once a foe has shown a spread move. Wacan Berry lets Celesteela survive the Thunder that used to kill it on turn one, and Beast Boost turns each KO into more Attack. Zapdos brings Thunderbolt, Hurricane and spread Heat Wave under the Tailwind. Altaria, Winona's signature, is the anchor that resets the sky. As a Dragon/Flying type it takes Electric only neutrally, and its Calm special bulk absorbs Thunder. It re-sets Tailwind once the old one expires, uses Helping Hand to power up a Superpower or Earthquake, and Ice Beams Electric/Flying, Grass, Ground and Dragon foes. Natural Cure and Roost keep it cycling. Reserves: Mega Skarmory is the separate endgame. Iron Defense into Body Press beats the physical Rock, Ice, Steel and Dark bodies. Rock Slide from its 140 base Attack hits the Fire and Electric flyers that answer Steel, and Brave Bird hits Grass and Fighting. AI executability: TAILWIND is Talonflame's turn-one move, and Altaria resets it. SETUP is Contrary Superpower plus Skarmory's Iron Defense. Wide Guard and Quick Guard turn on only after the player has shown a spread or priority move. Ace Pokemon keeps Mega Skarmory last. Could this be cooler? The first redesign won turn one only when Enamorus happened to outspeed the player's fastest lead. Below that tier it Protected, handed the player a free Mega Evolution turn, and died to Freeze-Dry. Now the gym's lesson (priority Tailwind) is Winona's own opening, and the player has to fight for the speed of the battle instead of reading one stat. Level offsets: Enamorus, Celesteela and Zapdos +2 as legend-class; Talonflame and Altaria +3; Mega Skarmory +1.
crack: Her Tailwind will go up on turn one, so plan around it rather than trying to stop it. Only Talonflame wears the Cloak: Fake Out still flinches Enamorus, and Enamorus has no answer to Electric, so Fake Out plus a strong Electric hit removes it before it moves. Matching her Tailwind with your own restores the normal speed order, Trick Room reverses it, and Protect or a switch wastes her four Tailwind turns. Don't lead Intimidate or Parting Shot into Contrary. Yache Berry absorbs only the first Ice hit on Enamorus, and Wacan Berry only the first Electric hit on Celesteela. Grassy Terrain halves Earthquake, Knock Off strips either berry, and Celesteela is slow once Tailwind ends. Rock hits Talonflame 4x and Zapdos 2x. Any chip damage takes away Gale Wings priority, and single-target moves get past Wide Guard. Taunt Altaria to stop the reset. Special Fire or Electric breaks Mega Skarmory before Iron Defense stacks, and Ghost-types ignore Body Press. Ice still hits Enamorus, Zapdos and Altaria (4x) super-effectively.

## E0300 TRAINER_CRISTIN_1 class=ace

Regieleki moves before almost anything and spends that first action on Reflect against a physical Ground or sand lead, or Electroweb when both foes can be slowed, so the Mega's Boomburst lands through a slowed or weakened board; Bug Buzz is the single-target Ground song and Dragon Pulse reaches the Flying and Levitate bodies the song cannot touch. Reserves & disruption: Ninetales is held in the back on purpose - Drought fires when it arrives, after the player's sand or rain setter has already used its entry, so the replacement takes the weather back instead of losing the turn-zero weather war; Heat Rock keeps the sun for eight turns. Ace Pokemon keeps Lilligant last, so it always enters into that sun: Chlorophyll doubles its Speed, Focus Sash buys one Sleep Powder or Leaf Storm, and Alluring Voice is its Fairy answer to the Dragons that wall Fire and Grass. Counterplay & audit: pop the Balloon with Rock Slide, Knock Off or any hit on Regieleki and the choir stops; Wide Guard or Protect blanks Boomburst; Flying and Levitate bodies are immune to it; Ice is four times effective on Mega Flygon; bring a second weather setter to take the field back after Ninetales. Could this team be cooler? The old build led Regieleki and Ninetales into a Ground spread move that killed both before either acted, and the sand then erased the sun for the rest of the fight. Now the Ground spread move belongs to Cristin: a Ground-type Boomburst sung over a floating Regieleki is something no other trainer does, the legendary has a job the player can see and break, and the sun arrives late on purpose so it wins the weather war instead of losing it on turn zero.
crack: Pop Regieleki's Air Balloon on turn one (Rock Slide, Knock Off, any hit) so Boomburst would hurt it and Flygon has to stop singing; Wide Guard or Protect the Boomburst turn; lead Flying or Levitate bodies that the Ground song cannot touch; Ice is four times effective on Mega Flygon; keep a second weather setter to retake the field after Ninetales arrives, and Knock Off Lilligant's Focus Sash.

## E0311 TRAINER_GABRIELLE_1 class=ace
strategy: SNOW,SETUP
mega_slots: 1
ai: Conservative
plan: First two useful turns: Mega Abomasnow's Snow Warning is automatic and snow raises the Defense of every Ice type on the field by 50 percent, so Gabrielle's whole team becomes physically bulkier the moment the battle starts. Alolan Sandslash's Slush Rush doubles its Speed in that snow and Cetitan's does the same, so the team has two sweepers running off one weather. Alternate deployment: Frosmoth's Ice Scales halves every special attack it takes, which is the answer to the Fire and Rock special coverage a player brings to an Ice team, and Quiver Dance behind that makes it the win condition. Reserves & disruption: Avalugg's Sturdy guarantees one survived hit and Body Press converts its 184 base Defense - already raised by snow - into damage; Mamoswine's Thick Fat halves the Fire and Ice attacks aimed at it and Ice Shard is the priority finish. Counterplay & audit: replace the weather and both Slush Rush sweepers halve, Fire and Fighting and Rock and Steel all bite, and Frosmoth folds instantly to physical damage. Could this team be cooler? The old build was flagged RAIN and SNOW at once and actually ran both - a Gorebyss using Rain Dance beside a Snow Warning Abomasnow, so the two engines deleted each other every time either resolved. That is a genuine strategic defect, not a flavour note. It is cooler now because it is one committed weather with two Slush Rush abusers, an Ice Scales special wall and a Body Press physical wall, and because Frosmoth and Cetitan are both first appearances in the campaign. Asked again after the revision: the team now has a real reason to be an ace-class fight instead of a pile of cold Pokemon.
crack: Change the weather and the team loses half its Speed; Fire, Fighting, Rock and Steel pressure; Frosmoth dies to any physical attack; Stealth Rock-style chip undoes Sturdy.

## E0317 TRAINER_GRUNT_MT_PYRE_2 class=grunt
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: The grave robbers, working the tomb floors, and everything in the crew is something they dug up. First two useful turns: the lead pair are both Ghosts, so the player's Fake Out does nothing to either of them, and both are built to punish the usual lead of Intimidate plus Knock Off. Annihilape's Defiant turns an Intimidate into +2 Attack, and its Drain Punch is four times effective on Tyranitar and Kingambit and super effective on Incineroar, so the Dark lead that blanks most Ghost teams feeds this one. Gholdengo's Good as Gold blocks every status move aimed at it - Parting Shot, Taunt, Encore, Spore, Thunder Wave - so its Nasty Plot cannot be disrupted the usual way; Make It Rain hits both foes and is super effective on Tyranitar and Fairies, Focus Blast is the Fighting answer to the Dark-Steel types that resist it, and a Colbur Berry halves the first Knock Off so it lives to act. Alternate deployment: Antique Polteageist waits in the back, away from the lead-slot Intimidate, and comes in to Shell Smash with its White Herb intact; Strength Sap heals it and cuts a physical attacker's Attack, and Giga Drain is its answer to the Rock and Water types. Reserves & disruption: Carracosta is the fossil they chiselled out of the mountain - Solid Rock softens super-effective hits, the Rocky Helmet punishes every contact Knock Off and Low Kick, its own Knock Off robs the player's item, and Aqua Jet finishes a weakened sweeper. The summit's permanent fog opens every battle with Misty Terrain, which blocks status on grounded targets, so the crew carries no status attack; its disruption is stat drops and stolen items, which the terrain does not block. Counterplay & audit: Ghost, Flying, Psychic and Fairy hit Annihilape hard and none of those trip Defiant; Ground, Fire and Ghost hit Gholdengo, and Good as Gold does nothing against plain damage; Polteageist's Herb is burned by any Intimidate or Parting Shot that lands before it smashes. Could this team be cooler? The previous block led Weavile, which a Fighting move deleted on turn one, and a Focus Sash Mismagius that Knock Off ignored, so the Shell Smash plan never ran. It is cooler now because it is a real haul: a rage-cursed ape that would not stay buried, a chest of coins that walked off with the robbers, an antique teapot and a fossil turtle, and the room's idea is that the tricks the player normally opens with - Fake Out, Intimidate, Parting Shot - are exactly what this crew feeds on.
crack: Do not lead Intimidate into Annihilape; hit it with Ghost, Flying, Psychic or Fairy instead. Fake Out cannot touch the lead, so spend turn one on damage: Ground, Fire or two hits on Gholdengo after its Colbur Berry. Keep an Intimidate or Parting Shot in reserve to pop Polteageist's White Herb when it arrives, or Knock Off the Herb first; a Dark type such as Incineroar or Kingambit resists Shadow Ball and walls Polteageist even after the Smash. Carracosta is slow and weak to Grass, Electric, Fighting and Ground - use non-contact moves to avoid the Rocky Helmet.

## E0318 TRAINER_GRUNT_MT_PYRE_3 class=grunt
