First two useful turns: Spiritomb has no weaknesses except Fairy and 35 base Speed, so it is the safest Trick Room setter in the region; it sets the room when the slow pair can spend it and uses Sucker Punch or Snarl otherwise, with Pressure draining the player's PP on the long turns and Pain Split keeping the setter alive for a second room. The summit's permanent fog opens every battle with Misty Terrain, which blocks burns and every other status on grounded targets, so the crew's disruption is stat drops rather than status: Snarl lowers both foes' Special Attack and Drifblim's Strength Sap lowers one foe's Attack while healing Drifblim, and the terrain blocks neither. Reserves & disruption: Drifblim's Aftermath punishes the contact knockout, Strength Sap is the physical deterrent Will-O-Wisp used to be, and Mystical Fire is the special one. Storm Drain instead of Rage Powder also means Safety Goggles - the player's usual answer - does nothing.
crack: Taunt or Fairy pressure on Spiritomb; the terrain means nothing here can burn or poison you, but Snarl and Strength Sap still shrink your attacks; spread Water moves bypass Storm Drain; Protect through the five turns; Ghost and Dark pressure on Drifblim.

Araquanid is the standout - a water-bubble spider is a genuinely strange, memorable thing for a pirate to keep, and doubled Water damage is the clearest possible statement that the rain is not decoration.
crack: Change the weather first; Electric and Rock pressure on Pelipper; Fairy and Psychic on Okidogi, and never lead Intimidate into it; Wide Guard and Protect blunt the spread turns; Golisopod's First Impression only works on its first turn out.

## E0336 TRAINER_GRUNT_MAGMA_HIDEOUT_13 class=grunt
strategy: SAND
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Room sixteen, the iron gate outside the admins' chamber, and the hardest grunt fight in the campaign so far. First two useful turns: Tyranitar's Sand Stream overwrites whatever weather the player installed in the last room - including the rain a player brings for a Rock and Steel gate - and its Assault Vest makes the special answer to it fail; it attacks immediately, and Ice Punch is there for the Ground or Flying lead that expects to walk through. Probopass' Magnet Pull traps the player's Steel switch-ins - the exact Pokemon a player brings to answer a Rock and Ground hideout - and its Rock/Steel body ignores the sand while Leftovers keeps it there. Alternate deployment: Steelix takes Wide Guard against the player's spread answer - the rain-boosted Surf and the Earthquake this gate invites - and Body Press converts its enormous Defense into damage. Reserves & disruption: Ferrothorn is the thorn in the gate and the answer to its obvious counter. Grass/Steel resists Water, takes Ground only neutrally and cannot be chipped by the sand, so the Water and Ground attackers that fold the other three meet a wall that Power Whips them for super-effective damage and Leech Seeds whatever stays; Iron Barbs punishes contact, Gyro Ball off its crawling Speed is the room's Steel damage into Fairy and Ice, and the Occa Berry means the one Fire attack the player saves for it takes two tries. That frees Probopass to carry Dazzling Gleam, a spread hit into the Fighting attackers the rest of the gate fears. Garchomp is absent here; this room deliberately has no fast member, so the player who solved earlier rooms with speed has to solve this one with damage. Counterplay & audit: Fighting still breaks all four if it survives the Gleam, Fire burns Ferrothorn through its berry, and Steel-typed players must be aware they cannot switch out; Water and Ground still work on Tyranitar, Steelix and Probopass once Ferrothorn is removed or ignored. Could this team be cooler? The old block was Rhyperior/Amoonguss/Pangoro/Tauros - a mushroom and a cow standing between the player and Maxie - and the first rebuild's Rhydon only repeated Tyranitar's Rock and Ground lane, so rain and a Landorus walked through all four. It is cooler now because it is a gate rather than a team: sand to undo the player's weather, a trap to punish the natural Steel answer, a wall that converts defence into offence, and a thorned iron bar across the Water and Ground answer everything else here fears. Trapping the player's Steel pivot with Magnet Pull immediately before the admin gauntlet is the most consequential grunt decision in the hideout.
crack: Do not bring a Steel pivot you need to rotate; Fire through Ferrothorn's Occa Berry, then Water and Ground into the other three; Fighting pressure once Probopass is gone; Taunt on Steelix and Ferrothorn; the room has no speed control, so fast special attackers dictate the pace.

Reserves & disruption: Mantine's Tailwind is the alternative to Wide Guard when the crew is behind on speed; Whiscash's Rock Slide covers the Flying Electric users that High Horsepower cannot touch. Counterplay & audit: chip Wailord before it Spouts; Grass is the clean answer now - four times on Whiscash and super-effective on Wailord; Electric still breaks Wailord and Mantine once Whiscash is removed or out of position; this is a straight damage race with no draining tricks. Could this team be cooler? The old block's third slot was Poipole, an Ultra Beast from another dimension standing in a pirate hideout, and the first rebuild's Tentacruel left three of four members Electric-weak, so a single Electric sweeper walked through the room. It is cooler now because every member is something you would actually find in a flooded hold - a whale, a catfish in the bilge water, an anchor and a manta - and because the room states the Aqua thesis in one move: act before Water Spout or lose both slots, and the catfish is waiting for the Electric answer. Mantine's Wide Guard also teaches the player early that this faction protects its spread turns.
crack: Chip or Fake Out Wailord before it Spouts; Grass pressure first (Whiscash is four-times weak), then Electric into Wailord and Mantine; Dhelmise is slow and folds to Fire and Dark; spread moves are answered by Wide Guard, so aim single-target on the turn you expect it.

## E0342 TRAINER_GRUNT_AQUA_HIDEOUT_3 class=grunt
strategy: SETUP,ALLY_COMBO

The old room led Seismitoad, a fourth Grass-weak shell that spent the setup turn on Protect, beside a Barbaracle that was Fake Outed and Close Combatted before it ever moved; the Smash plan never ran once in three benchmark games. It is cooler now because the crew answers the exact question every expert asks it: the lookout grinds its teeth, the terrain hums, and the player's Fake Out bounces off - the room still can be beaten, but only by committing both hands to the breaker on turn one or by winning the terrain back.
crack: Double Barbaracle on turn one (Focus Sash only stops one hit) or spread-hit it once Toxapex is gone; switch in a Surge ability to replace Psychic Terrain and reopen priority; Tailwind or a Choice Scarf outspeeds +2 Barbaracle; Grass and Electric take Bruxish, Water or Rock take the ungrounded Rotom-Heat, and Electric or Ground break Toxapex.

Reserves & disruption: Tsareena's Queenly Majesty blocks every priority move aimed at this side - Fake Out, Gale Wings, Sucker Punch, Extreme Speed - while the team's own Grassy Glide keeps its priority, so in terrain only this side gets to move first. crack: All four attack physically - Intimidate, Will-O-Wisp and Attack drops; Water, Ground, Fighting or Grass on Relicanth after Sturdy is broken; Ice or Psychic spread into the three Grass and Flying members; your own Wide Guard blanks both Rock Slides; replace the terrain; Hawlucha is frail, so remove it before it gets a free Swords Dance.

## E0389 TRAINER_VIRGIL class=gym
strategy: TRICK_ROOM
mega_slots: 6
plan: Room two: the reversal - the gym's one dedicated Trick Room, and the one room whose setters cannot be stopped by the usual tool. Dark answer: Armor Tail, then Speed reversed. First two useful turns: Farigiraf and Hatterene lead as two setters. Farigiraf's Armor Tail makes every priority move aimed at Virgil's side fail - Fake Out, Sucker Punch, Ice Shard, Bullet Punch, Grassy Glide, Gale Wings and Prankster Taunt alike - so the counter-party's normal way of stopping a setter on turn one does not exist here, and Hatterene's Magic Bounce returns an ordinary Taunt. The AI sets the room when its side is the slower one, which against this gym's counters is almost always; if the player focuses one setter, the other finishes the job, and Reuniclus is a third setter for the re-set. Alternate deployment: inside the room Hatterene (29 base Speed, Speed IV 0) and Reuniclus (30) move before every Dark type in the region. Hatterene's Life Orb Dazzling Gleam hits Tyranitar, Weavile and Meowscarada super-effectively and Mystical Fire burns through Kingambit, Gholdengo and Scizor while cutting their Special Attack; Reuniclus has Magic Guard, so Life Orb, sand and Rocky Helmet cost it nothing, Focus Blast is its Dark answer and Shadow Ball its Ghost answer. Hariyama, the one non-Psychic, is the room's anchor: Fake Out, Close Combat into Kingambit and Tyranitar, Heavy Slam at full 120 power into Flutter Mane, Thick Fat against Flare Blitz and Heat Wave, and Wide Guard against the Rock Slide and Make It Rain that would otherwise sweep a slow board. Reserves & disruption: Chimecho's Snarl takes a stage of Special Attack off both foes before they move under the room, Knock Off strips a Life Orb or Assault Vest and Helping Hand doubles the next room hit. The room ends after five turns, and Mega Medicham is the answer to waiting it out: Pure Power doubles its Attack, Jolly max Speed makes it fast once normal order returns, Fake Out and Bullet Punch move first inside or outside the room (Bullet Punch is its Flutter Mane answer) and High Jump Kick ends Kingambit and Tyranitar. Counterplay & audit: Armor Tail does not stop spread damage, a non-priority Taunt into Farigiraf, or two big hits into one setter before the room resolves; Make It Rain into Hatterene is the cleanest single hit; Protect and switch through the five turns, then outspeed or tank Medicham with Flying, Fairy or Psychic hits (Ghosts ignore its Fake Out and Fighting moves); Wide Guard is a turn Hariyama does not attack. Could this team be cooler? The old room's Bronzong was Eli's exact Lavaridge setter and died to Fake Out plus Knock Off before Trick Room ever went up, so Medicham never got a second move. It is cooler now because the obvious answer - priority - is switched off, and the team has a plan for both halves of the fight: the room, and the moment it ends. Asked again: Hariyama earns the off-type slot because it is the right shape for a reversed room (slow, Fake Out, Wide Guard, Thick Fat) and gives the room the Flutter Mane answer no slow Psychic has.
crack: Make It Rain, Shadow Ball and other special Ghost or Steel hits on Hatterene and Reuniclus; double-target one setter only when the other is already down; stall the room with Protect and switches, then outspeed or tank Mega Medicham (Flying, Fairy, Psychic; Ghost types ignore its Fake Out and Fighting); non-priority Taunt on Farigiraf; Hariyama's Wide Guard turns are free turns for single-target attacks.

## E0390 TRAINER_BLAKE class=gym
strategy: MEGA_REVEAL
mega_slots: 6
plan: Room three: the barrier. Blake answers the Dark type with walls it cannot argue with and a punishment for the one disruption it always brings. Dark answer: Prankster screens plus Competitive. First two useful turns: the male Meowstic leads with Prankster Reflect and Light Screen (Light Clay, eight turns). Screens target Blake's own side, so the rule that Prankster status moves fail against Dark types never applies to them, and the same body's Fake Out covers the turn they go up. Mr. Mime, the Barrier Pokemon, stands beside it: Filter takes a quarter off every super-effective hit on top of the screens, Wide Guard blanks Rock Slide, Make It Rain and Heat Wave for both slots, and Dazzling Gleam and Mystical Fire are its Dark and Steel answers. Alternate deployment: Gothitelle and the female Meowstic both have Competitive, so the Intimidate or Parting Shot that every Incineroar lead brings hands them +2 Special Attack for each stat it lowers. Could this team be cooler? The old room's female Meowstic had nothing that could touch a Dark type, Ally Switch was never used, and a double-Dark lead broke the screens and folded the room. It is cooler now because every piece is a wall with a counterattack: the screens the Dark type cannot stop, the Competitive bodies its Intimidate feeds, and a Huge Power Starmie that hits from behind the barrier. Asked again: Armor Tail Farigiraf moved to Virgil's room, where it protects a setter rather than duplicating what the screens already do.
crack: Brick Break, Psychic Fangs, Defog or Infiltrator against the screens; never feed Intimidate or Parting Shot to Gothitelle or the female Meowstic; spread damage beats Mr. Mime's single-turn Wide Guard on the turns it attacks; Electric, Grass and Dark special attacks on Mega Starmie once Light Screen is down; Steel and Ghost attacks on the Fairy and Psychic bodies.

The old room was five pure Psychic attackers whose setup never fired; Mega Tyranitar's Crunch removed them one per turn and +30 levels could not save it. It is cooler now because the room changes what the Dark types can do rather than trying to outlast them, and because Pyromancy is a mechanic no other room in Hoenn uses. Asked again: two foxes rather than one - Delphox the Psychic fox and Ninetales the mystic fox - so removing one fire does not put the hearth out.
crack: Special attackers and Fire types are immune to the plan - Gholdengo, Flutter Mane, Chi-Yu, Incineroar; Water, Rock and Ground hits on Ninetales and Delphox; Sucker Punch or Knock Off into Delphox before it fires; Fake Out Ninetales on the turn Indeedee cannot cover it; Lum Berry, Guts or Flare Boost turn a burn into nothing.

Asked again: Gothitelle moved to Blake's room as a Competitive wall, so Shadow Tag appears in exactly one room.

## E0395 TRAINER_NATE class=gym
strategy: NONE
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Room eight: the mesmerist. Nate is the gym's stage hypnotist, and his answer to Dark types is that they stop choosing their own moves. Dark answer: Encore, Disable and Taunt without Prankster, so the Dark type's immunity to Prankster status never applies, from bodies Fake Out and Intimidate cannot touch. First two useful turns: Hypno and Oranguru lead. Both have Inner Focus, so Fake Out cannot flinch them and Intimidate does not lower them. Hypno Encores whatever the player just used: a Fake Out then fails for three turns, a Protect fails on its second use, and a Sucker Punch fails whenever its target uses a status move; its Focus Blast is the Kingambit and Tyranitar answer and Dazzling Gleam the Weavile and Meowscarada answer. Oranguru Taunts the Parting Shot, Trick Room, screens, Tailwind or Nasty Plot and Knock Offs the Life Orb or Assault Vest. Alternate deployment: Alakazam is the third Inner Focus mentalist and the fastest member: it Disables the move that would knock out its partner, then fires Life Orb Focus Blast, Shadow Ball and Dazzling Gleam. Reserves & disruption: Wyrdeer's antlers are the hypnotist's pendulum - Clear Amulet means Intimidate cannot touch it either, Psyshield Bash raises its Defense, Megahorn is the Bug answer to Dark and High Horsepower the Ground answer to Kingambit, Incineroar and Gholdengo. Orbeetle's Struggle Bug lowers both foes' Special Attack, Bug Buzz hits Dark types and Rocky Helmet punishes contact on its 110 Defense; Alolan Exeggutor's Harvest recycles its Sitrus Berry while Flamethrower answers Steel types and Draco Meteor anything else. Counterplay & audit: attack rather than use the moves Encore wants - Encore only locks the last move, and locking an attack into an attack gains Nate little; switching clears Encore and Disable; Gholdengo's Good as Gold blocks Encore, Disable and Taunt outright; special Ghost and Dark hits on Hypno and Alakazam; Sucker Punch is punished, ordinary attacks are not. The AI must never Encore a foe that has not moved yet, and never Disable a move that is already disabled. Could this team be cooler? The old room's Oranguru-Instruct-Delphox engine was a copy of Eli's Oranguru Instruct in Lavaridge, and Delphox died on turn two without ever being Instructed. It is cooler now because the room fights the player's choices rather than their typing, and the three Inner Focus bodies make the counter-party's Fake Out and Intimidate - the two things it always brings - do nothing. ## E0403 TRAINER_GRUNT_SPACE_CENTER_4 class=grunt
strategy: REDIRECTION,ALLY_COMBO
mega_slots: NONE
plan: The magnet bay is the space centre's electromagnetic launch rail, a mass driver that throws payloads at orbit, and Magma has put the rail's own crew to work: two railguns, the coolant plant and the moon Clefable the centre keeps for luck. Every member of this room either floats over the rail or shields it. First two useful turns: Alolan Golem leads and is the bay's shield. Covert Cloak means Fake Out cannot flinch it, so its Wide Guard always goes up on turn one, before Water Spout, Origin Pulse, Earthquake, Precipice Blades, Eruption or any other spread move. Rotom-Wash, the Rotom living in the rail's water-cooling plant, stands beside it. Rotom resists Water, Fire, Ice and Steel, and Levitate takes it out of the way of Ground moves, so between them nothing the player sends into the lead pair hits hard. Rotom's Thunderbolt punishes Water leads, its Hydro Pump hits the Ground, Fire and Rock answers and gets stronger in the player's own rain, and Will-O-Wisp burns the physical attacker. Once the spread threat is spent, Golem attacks. Galvanize turns Double-Edge into an Electric railgun shot, and its Earthquake shakes the whole floor while both floating crewmates take nothing. Alternate deployment: Vikavolt is the second railgun, and Levitate lets it hover over Golem's Earthquake as well; it outspeeds Kyogre, Groudon and Mega Garchomp and fires Thunderbolt, Energy Ball for the Water and Ground counters, and Bug Buzz. Reserves & disruption: Clefable is the narrow-lane half of the shield. Follow Me pulls the single-target Ground, Fighting and Grass hits that Wide Guard cannot stop off Golem, Moonblast answers Dragons, Fighting types and Incineroar, Ice Beam hits the Ground and Flying types, and Unaware ignores the player's boosts. Clefable is the one grounded crewmate, so Golem uses Rock Slide or Galvanize Double-Edge beside it instead of Earthquake. Counterplay & audit: the shield stops spread moves only; Feint lifts Wide Guard, single-target Grass, Ground and Fighting moves all hit Golem super effectively, Grass is Rotom-Wash's only weakness, and Fire and Rock remove Vikavolt. Could this team be cooler? The old block was Gravity plus sure-hit Blizzard, the same room Nicholas built two fights earlier, and its Probopass lead was weak to Water, Ground and Fighting, so Fake Out plus rain Water Spout removed the setter on turn one every time and the plan never started. It is cooler now because the bay plays like a launch rail: one magnetic shield that switches off the player's biggest spread move, two railguns that float over their own Earthquake, and a coolant Rotom whose Hydro Pump gets stronger in the rain the player brought to beat it.
crack: Feint breaks Wide Guard, and single-target moves are never blocked: Grass hits Golem and Rotom-Wash, single-target Ground and Fighting hit Golem four and two times over, and Fire or Rock removes Vikavolt. Clefable's Follow Me draws single-target hits, so spread damage or a Steel or Poison attack on Clefable comes first. Golem is slow and has no recovery, so taking it out ends both the shield and the Earthquake. Do not bring rain without a plan, because Rotom's Hydro Pump is stronger in it.

## E0405 TRAINER_GRUNT_SPACE_CENTER_5 class=grunt
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: The control room, held by infiltrators. First two useful turns: Zoroark enters disguised as the last member of the party - the player sees Shiftry and targets Shiftry, and the attack lands on a 60/40/40 Dark type instead. The illusion breaks the moment Zoroark is hit, so the crew's plan is to use that one turn of misdirection on Kingambit's Swords Dance. Alternate deployment: Kingambit's Supreme Overlord raises its Attack by 10 percent for every fallen ally, so it is deliberately placed to come in late; Kowtow Cleave never misses and Sucker Punch closes. Reserves & disruption: Cacturne's Water Absorb heals on the Water attacks the player packed for a Fire-and-Rock faction, and Sucker Punch gives the room a second priority lane. Could this team be cooler? The old block was Reuniclus, Pangoro, Nidoking and Sandaconda - a Trick Room setter with three unrelated bruisers and no reason to be at a space centre. It is cooler now because infiltration is the correct idea for the room where Magma takes the controls: an Illusion that costs the player a turn, then a Dark/Steel general who gets stronger every time the player wins an exchange. The two mechanics point the same way - the longer the fight runs, the worse the board gets - and the counterplay, a single spread move, is clean and fair.
crack: One spread move breaks the illusion and reveals the board; Fighting and Fire pressure on Kingambit, with the Fighting type kept away from Shiftry's Air Slash - a Fairy type hits three of the four super-effectively and fears only Kingambit's Iron Head; do not Water-attack Cacturne; remove Kingambit before its allies fall rather than after.

## E0407 TRAINER_GRUNT_SPACE_CENTER_7 class=grunt
strategy: NONE
mega_slots: NONE
plan: The launch pad, and the last grunt before Tabitha - the hardest non-admin fight in the villain arc. The crew holding it is built from the pad itself: the weather balloon that goes up before every launch, the alloy service tower, the meteorite payload Maxie's whole plot is about, and a volcano cannon that launches fire. First two useful turns: Drifblim and Duraludon lead because each covers the other. Drifblim is Ghost and Flying, so Fake Out cannot touch it and Ground and Fighting attacks pass straight through it - the two types Duraludon fears - while Duraludon resists the Rock and Electric attacks that threaten the balloon; no spread move hits both of them super effectively. Fake Out and spread Ground can only go into Duraludon, and Eviolite on a full-HP-invested Duraludon now survives a Life Orb Precipice Blades from full. Drifblim is faster than an Adamant Groudon and spends turn one on Will-O-Wisp on the biggest physical threat or Icy Wind across both foes; after Icy Wind the slow tower outruns a slowed Groudon or Arcanine and fires Draco Meteor, Flash Cannon or Thunderbolt, and Drifblim's Helping Hand on that Draco Meteor is the room's knockout line. Stalwart means the player's Follow Me or Rage Powder cannot pull that shot away from its target. Alternate deployment: Drifblim's Sitrus Berry pays for one hit and Unburden then doubles its Speed, and Strength Sap lowers a physical attacker's Attack while healing the balloon by that Attack. Reserves & disruption: Metagross is the meteorite, and its Weakness Policy is re-entry heat - the Fire or Ground hit that should finish it raises its Attack two stages instead, and Meteor Mash, Ice Punch into the Ground and Dragon attackers, Stomping Tantrum into Fire and Steel, and Bullet Punch then follow. Magmortar is the launcher: in this build it can carry Mega Launcher, so its Aura Sphere and Dark Pulse hit at 1.5 times their power beside a sun-boosted Heat Wave, and a player who brings Drought to break the Steel types is fuelling Magma's cannon. Counterplay & audit: Dark, Ghost, Rock, Ice and Electric attacks remove the balloon, and with the balloon gone spread Ground hits the Steels again; the back pair of Metagross and Magmortar shares the Ground weakness, so the room is won by taking Drifblim out first and keeping a Ground attacker healthy for the end. Could this team be cooler? The old lead put two Ground-weak Steels side by side into Fake Out plus Precipice Blades, so Duraludon died before it ever acted and the Storm Drain Cradily repeated a fossil-maniac gimmick from much earlier. It is cooler now because every member is a piece of the launch: the balloon that tests the wind shields the tower from the ground, the meteorite gets hotter when struck, and the volcano Pokemon whose arm is a cannon fires the payload.
crack: Kill or disable Drifblim first with Dark, Ghost, Rock, Ice or Electric attacks - Fake Out does nothing to it - and then spread Ground and Fighting hit Duraludon and Metagross again; Fire and Ground still answer the Steels and Water, Ground and Rock answer Magmortar, which shares the Ground weakness with Metagross at the end; do not feed Metagross a weak super-effective hit that only triggers Weakness Policy; Duraludon ignores redirection, so Protect or Wide Guard the target instead.

## E0408 TRAINER_TABITHA_MOSSDEEP class=admin
strategy: ALLY_COMBO
mega_slots: 3
ai: Ace Pokemon
plan: Tabitha came to the Space Center for the rocket fuel, and on this floor he has lit it. There is no weather plan: the hideout raised a sandstorm and the admins upstairs bring Mega Charizard's sun, but this fight is a launch sequence built from the station's own machinery and Magma's fire, and the only Pokémon it shares with his hideout crew are Coalossal and his foreman Krookodile. First two useful turns: Iron Hands and Coalossal lead. Iron Hands is the gantry's heavy-lift machine the raid hot-wired. Fake Out flinches one foe on turn one, its Assault Vest takes a Life Orb rain Water Spout from full for about two-thirds to three-quarters of its HP, and at full Attack Wild Charge knocks out a Kyogre with no Defense investment from full HP and any Pelipper; Drain Punch is the answer to Incineroar, Tyranitar and Kingambit, Ice Punch to Garchomp, Landorus and Rayquaza. Coalossal is the booster: Calm with full Special Defense it survives the same Water Spout, the custom Steam Engine caps Water at neutral and turns that hit into +6 Speed, and from then on it outruns almost anything that is not under Tailwind or Swift Swim. Its new job is the stolen fuel - Tar Shot lowers the target's Speed and makes every Fire hit on it count double for as long as it stays in, so a tarred Kyogre takes Fire at neutral and a tarred Rillaboom, Amoonguss or Gholdengo takes it at four times; Will-O-Wisp burns the physical counter and Heat Wave chips both slots. Alternate deployment: Mega Scovillain is the heat shield, the chemist that turns fuel into fire. Grass/Fire is neutral to Water and Ground, takes Grass at a quarter and ignores Spore and Rage Powder, and Spicy Spray burns every Pokémon that damages it and can be burned - Water Spout and Precipice Blades included - so a physical Water or Ground answer that touches it fights at half Attack for the rest of the battle. Grass Knot is 120 power into Kyogre, Groudon, Great Tusk and Tyranitar and knocks out most Kyogre in one hit, Leaf Storm is the burst for targets too light for Grass Knot, and Flamethrower punishes Grass and Steel. Reserves & disruption: Orthworm is the tunnel the crew came in through. Earth Eater turns any Ground hit into a quarter of its HP, so Krookodile's Earthquake hits both foes and heals it, Helping Hand primes whichever partner is about to fire, Body Press off its armored Defense answers Incineroar and Kingambit, and Heavy Slam answers the Fairy types that threaten Iron Hands and Krookodile. Krookodile returns from the hideout as the foreman: Intimidate on entry, Knock Off strips Assault Vests and Sitrus Berries, Rock Slide reaches Pelipper and Charizard. Typhlosion, the Volcano Pokémon, is the ignition he holds back to the end: Rampage, an Inclement Ability, skips Blast Burn's recharge whenever the hit knocks its target out, so a chipped or tarred board takes a 150-power Fire hit every turn; Heat Wave covers both slots and Scorching Sands reaches the Fire, Steel and Electric answers. Counterplay & audit: rain still halves every Fire move on this team, so rain is a fair plan when it also removes Iron Hands and Scovillain - Ground, Psychic or Fairy into Iron Hands, and a Fire type or a special attacker into Scovillain, because Fire types cannot be burned and burn costs a special attacker nothing. Intimidate drops Wild Charge below the Kyogre knockout; never feed Coalossal Water or Fire unless the hit kills it, and use Ground (4x) or Fighting instead; kill Orthworm with Fire or Fighting, never Ground; switch a tarred Pokémon out to wash the tar off; a Blast Burn that does not knock its target out leaves Typhlosion recharging, and Water, Ground and Rock all hit it hard. Could this team be cooler? The old build was a sand team that copied his hideout - four of the same species, a Landorus four-times weak to the Ice Beam that came every game, a Magnet Pull Magnezone copied from Wattson and a Sand Rush plan the Mega Excadrill never had - and the first redesign fixed the rain collapse by rebuilding that same hideout. It is cooler now because this floor is its own fight with no weather, no Wide Guard and no Booster Energy to repeat the grunts below or Courtney and Maxie above: the station's machine holds the clamp, Coalossal pours the fuel and rides the steam, the heat shield sets every attacker alight, the worm drinks its own crew's quake, and the Volcano Pokémon fires without pause. Asked again: the ignition comes last because a launch countdown ends with it.
crack: Fake Out or Intimidate Iron Hands, then Ground, Psychic or Fairy; Fire types or special attackers into Mega Scovillain, never physical non-Fire hits; Ground (4x) or Fighting on Coalossal and no Water or Fire into it; Fire or Fighting on Orthworm, never Ground; switch out of Tar Shot; rain halves every Fire move; survive or redirect Typhlosion's Blast Burn so it recharges, then Water, Ground or Rock.

crack: Switch your Drizzle user out and back in after Charizard has Mega Evolved; Rock (4x) and Electric into Mega Charizard Y; Wide Guard the turn-one Heat Wave and Eruption; Ground and Water into Heatran; Fairy, Flying and Psychic into Great Tusk.

## E0410 TRAINER_SOPHIA class=ace
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Concept: a Grassy Terrain dance troupe. Tapu Bulu's Grassy Surge is the stage; Bellossom dances on it and Oricorio's Dancer copies every dance the instant it is performed. First two useful turns: Bellossom opens with Quiver Dance or Petal Dance while Tapu Bulu attacks; Oricorio's Dancer copies the dance for free, so one turn buys two boosted special attackers. Turn two spends the real boosts instead of stacking a third dance. Alternate deployment: when powder or Fire pressure denies the troupe, Mudsdale's Stamina/Body Press mode and Tapu Bulu's Horn Leech carry the fight with no setup. Yes, and it now is: the old Contrary Lurantis was a solo stat-trick that Oricorio's Dancer could never touch, so the team's signature ability did nothing. Lurantis is retained by Vito (E0487) so nothing is lost; Bellossom and Oricorio-Pom-Pom appear nowhere else in the campaign, and Mudsdale's other owner Herman (E0422) is retooled to Copperajah. Levels: cap 76, offsets 1/1/1/2 - the Mudsdale anchor pays for the two fragile dancers.
crack: Break the dance on turn one: Taunt or Encore Bellossom, or knock it out before Oricorio can copy. Fire, Flying and Ice attacks punish the whole troupe, Haze erases both copies at once, and terrain replacement removes Bulu's healing. Mudsdale folds to special attacks despite the Assault Vest.

## E0422 TRAINER_HERMAN class=ace
strategy: TRICK_ROOM,SETUP
mega_slots: 6
plan: Concept: a Trick Room Cooltrainer on the open sea below Sky Pillar who has lost to every cheap answer to Trick Room and packed a reply to each one: a Ghost setter that Fake Out cannot touch, a Mental Herb against the first Taunt, a salt-crusted Rock lead that eats Fire and punishes the sun, sea mist that refuses sleep and burns, and a second bell to set the room again. Every member runs zero Speed IVs and a Speed-lowering nature. First two useful turns: Dusknoir sets Trick Room on turn one - it is a Ghost, so a lead Fake Out cannot touch it, and Mental Herb cures the first Taunt or Encore - while Garganacl attacks. Purifying Salt makes Garganacl immune to status and halves Ghost damage, its Rock typing resists Fire, Flying and Fake Out, and Rock Slide is four times effective on Charizard, Talonflame and Volcarona, so a sun Heat Wave lead loses its attacker on the first turn instead of sweeping. Salt Cure on a Steel or Water foe costs it a quarter of its HP every turn. Turn two spends the room on damage: Dusknoir's Iron Fist Ice Punch and Fire Punch cover Garchomp, Amoonguss and Steel types, and Poltergeist covers the Ghosts. Alternate deployment: Florges' Misty Surge lays sea mist over the field, so grounded Pokemon on both sides cannot be put to sleep, burned, poisoned or paralysed and Dragon attacks on grounded targets are halved, which shuts off Spore, Yawn and Will-O-Wisp against Copperajah and Crabominable; Florges itself builds Calm Mind behind Wish and Protect as the special attacker that Intimidate cannot weaken. Reserves & disruption: Heatproof Bronzong is the second setter; it halves Fire damage, so the Fire-weak Steel bell now takes Fire attacks at neutral, and it resets the room when the first one ends, uses Helping Hand to push Copperajah or Crabominable through a knockout, and hits fast Pokemon hard with Gyro Ball. Copperajah's Heavy Metal doubles its weight for Heavy Slam and High Horsepower hits Fire and Steel types. Mega Crabominable is the payoff: Iron Fist Ice Hammer and Drain Punch under the reversed order, and Knock Off for the Ghost types that ignore its Fighting moves. AI executability: TRICK_ROOM is backed by Dusknoir and Bronzong; SETUP by Calm Mind. Could this team be cooler? The old block had the right idea and the wrong bodies: five of its six members were weak to Fire, and the setter was a Bronzong that Fake Out flinched on turn one, so Mega Charizard Y's Heat Wave plus one Fake Out beat the whole team before the room went up. Gourgeist, which never acted in any attempt, becomes Dusknoir, an unused Ghost that is naturally immune to Fake Out and gets Inclement's Iron Fist to match Mega Crabominable's. Heracross, weak to Flying and Fire, becomes Garganacl, a sea-salt Rock type that resists both. Florges gets its Inclement Misty Surge instead of Flower Veil, which did nothing on a team with no Grass type. Bronzong swaps Levitate for Heatproof and Hypnosis for Helping Hand, because sea mist would stop its own Hypnosis on any grounded target. Overrepresented? Dusknoir appears nowhere else; Garganacl's only other owners are the defensive Body Press walls of Dillon (E0115) and Roman (E0159); Misty Surge on Florges is unique; Warren (E0439) protects his setter with Covert Cloak and Conor (E0442) uses Gothitelle and Shadow Tag, so neither copies this. Levels: offsets 1/1/1/1/1/2.
crack: Hit the setter with two attacks on turn one: Dusknoir has little HP and takes double damage from Dark and Ghost moves, and its Mental Herb only stops the first Taunt, so a second Taunt, Imprison or your own Trick Room still denies the room. Lead with something Garganacl cannot hurt and hit it with Water, Grass, Ground, Fighting or Steel attacks; Gholdengo's Make It Rain is super effective on Garganacl, Florges and Crabominable at once. Almost the whole team is physical, so Intimidate cuts its damage, and sea mist only exists for five turns after Florges comes in. Copperajah and Crabominable are still weak to Fire, and once the room ends everything is slow again.

## E0433 TRAINER_DARCY class=ace
strategy: SUN,SETUP
mega_slots: 4
ai: Ace Pokemon
tactic: AFTER_YOU LILLIGANT AFTER_YOU TORKOAL
plan: Concept: the advanced student's answer to Flannery - the same After You plus Eruption idea, but with a second sun setter so the player cannot simply erase the weather once. First two useful turns: the authored tactic makes Lilligant offer After You to Torkoal when that actually lands a full-power Eruption before the opposing threats move; otherwise Lilligant uses Sleep Powder or Leaf Storm and Torkoal attacks in its own slow order. Turn two rechecks Torkoal's current HP, because Eruption scales with it, and whether the ally has already acted - After You is worthless then. Alternate deployment: Lilligant's sleep and support enable Porygon-Z's Adaptability Tri Attack or a Nasty Plot turn when the sun has been taken away. Reserves & disruption: Mega Charizard Y is the second real Drought, so Lilligant's manual Sunny Day is an emergency reclaim, not mandatory redundancy; Chlorophyll only doubles Lilligant's Speed while sun is actually up. Could this team be cooler? The idea was already strong but it was not executable - the block described an After You engine that no tactic line told the AI to perform, so in play it was a generic sun team. Adding the explicit AFTER_YOU tactic is what turns the concept into the fight the prose promises, and the weather-reclaim second setter is exactly the escalation a post-Flannery sun trainer should have. strategy: TAILWIND
mega_slots: 4
ai: Ace Pokemon
plan: Concept: the keeper of the Sealed Chamber's current - Marley dives the Route 134 trench, and she brought its guardian up with her. Her team is built in two halves that cover each other: a lead that shrugs off Fire and Flying, and a Grass back line that shrugs off the Water, Electric and Ground attacks a player brings to beat that lead. First two useful turns: Talonflame's Gale Wings gives its Flying moves priority while it is at full HP, so on turn one it either fires Brave Bird first at the biggest threat or puts up Tailwind first, and Regirock throws Rock Slide into both foes - Fire and Flying bodies take double or quadruple damage, and under Tailwind the 30% flinch lands before the foe can act. Venusaur trades Protect for Earth Power, so the Fire and Steel types sent to beat it take super-effective damage back. The two halves now cover each other's weaknesses: no attacking type hits more than two members super-effectively, Fire and Flying (which hit the Grass pair) are resisted by both leads, and Water (which hits both leads) is resisted by both Grass members. crack: Talonflame loses its priority once it is below full HP: chip it with anything, including Rough Skin, Rocky Helmet or a spread hit, then finish it with Rock or Electric. Fake Out on Talonflame stops its turn-one priority attack. Regirock's Defence is enormous but its Special Defence is ordinary, so hit it with special Water, Fighting, Ground or Grass attacks, and Ghost types ignore Body Press. Safety Goggles, Grass types and Electric or Misty Terrain stop Sleep Powder. Bulletproof covers ball and bomb moves only. Tailwind lasts four turns, so Protect through it or set your own speed control.

## E0459 TRAINER_ANDREA class=gym
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Concept: room one of eleven - the volley room. Sootopolis opens by teaching the player that a Water gym can simply out-damage them, with multi-hit attacks that ignore Substitutes, Focus Sashes and Sturdy. First two useful turns: Cloyster uses Shell Smash only when Floatzel's Choice Band damage buys it a survivable turn; otherwise both simply attack, because Skill Link Icicle Spear at five hits is already close to a boosted attack. Turn two handles Wave Crash recoil, the Sash and opposing priority before committing the boosted Cloyster, whose Drill Run backs up the room's Electric answers - the Sash is its protection, so Protect gave way for it. Mamoswine is the Ground one: immune to Electric, Loaded Dice Icicle Spear keeps the volley lesson at four or five hits and hits Electric/Dragons twice over, High Horsepower punishes the Electric/Fighting and Electric/Steel types, Thick Fat blunts the Fire hit aimed at its Ice half, and Ice Shard finishes what the volley leaves. Its weakness is a Fighting attack, and that is exactly what Dragapult cannot be hit by. Dragon/Ghost typing makes Dragapult immune to Fake Out and to every Fighting move and resists Electric, so an Electric/Fighting attacker's whole lead turn passes through it; Will-O-Wisp burns that attacker before its Drain Punch reaches Mamoswine, Dragon Darts fires two shots that hit an Electric/Dragon for double each, and Haban Berry halves the first Draco Meteor aimed back at it. Dragon Darts splits one dart onto each foe, or sends both into one when the other is protected or immune, so the volley lesson reaches both sides of the board, and Infiltrator carries it through Substitutes and screens the way Skill Link carries it through Sashes. Dreepy are said to haunt the prehistoric seas they lived in, and Sootopolis is a crater that the old sea filled - the room's volley ends with the Pokemon that launches its own young like missiles. U-turn gives Dragapult a way out once the Electric pair is handled. Simipour's special coverage covers the Grass types the rest of the room fears with Grass Knot. Reserves & disruption: Jellicent's Water Absorb, Will-O-Wisp and Recover is the attrition lane and the room's only recovery. Could this team be cooler? The Water spread and the multi-hit lesson are the right opening note for the gym, so the composition earns retention, but the Electric answer was a single point of failure: an Electric/Dragon legend beside an Electric/Fighting Paradox Fake Outed the lead, Drain Punched Mamoswine on its first turn and swept the rest in three. Basculin was Floatzel's lane twice over - Wave Crash and Aqua Jet on both - so its slot goes to the partner that turns the Fighting half of that pair into nothing. Simipour is the one member worth defending explicitly - a Torrent monkey looks like filler, but it is the room's special answer to an opposing Grass lead, and removing it would make the room one-dimensional. Overrepresented? Dragapult appears nowhere else in the game; Cloyster, Floatzel and Simipour appear only here; Jellicent and Mamoswine each have one distant other owner in different roles; Basculin leaves the game's trainer pool; no other Sootopolis room runs Shell Smash as its headline - Olivia's Carracosta uses a Weakness Policy version with the opposite risk profile.
crack: Electric attacks no longer cover the room: Mamoswine is immune and Dragapult resists them, so remove the pair with different tools - Water, Grass, Fighting or Steel attacks for Mamoswine (Thick Fat takes the sting out of Fire), and Ice, Dark, Ghost, Fairy or a second Dragon attack for Dragapult once its Haban Berry is spent; Heavy Slam from a heavy Steel type still hits it hard. A smashed Cloyster's Drill Run punishes the Electric type too, so break its Sash with a multi-hit or spread move. Grass attacks still hit five of six. Cloyster is physically bulky and specially fragile, so answer it on the special side before it smashes; priority finishes Floatzel after Wave Crash recoil. Will-O-Wisp on Jellicent and Dragapult is the room's only disruption, so a Fire type or a special attacker ignores it entirely.

## E0460 TRAINER_CRISSY class=gym
strategy: RAIN
mega_slots: NONE
ai: Conservative
plan: Concept: room two - the squall room, where the rain is made by hand and three different bodies are built to live inside it. First two useful turns: Swanna sets Rain Dance when its own Weather Ball - which becomes a 100-power Water attack in rain - and Lanturn's pressure both profit; Hydration then cures Swanna's status at the end of every rainy turn, so status is not an answer to it. Lanturn attacks or Volt Switches into the right body. Turn two exploits the actual weather rather than assuming every Water member needs it. Alternate deployment: Alomomola's Regenerator bulk and Mantine-free support line covers Choice Specs Primarina, whose Liquid Voice turns Hyper Voice into a spread Water attack that hits both opposing slots - the room's biggest single click. Reserves & disruption: Wishiwashi is only dangerous in School Form, which requires it to be above one quarter HP at level 20 or higher, so damaging it below that threshold reverts it to a nearly harmless fish mid-fight; Golisopod's Emergency Exit force-switches it at half HP, which interacts badly with its own Choice Band lock and is a real, visible weakness. Could this team be cooler? The room's best feature is that three of its six change form or state mid-battle - Schooling, Emergency Exit and rain-dependent Weather Ball - so the board the player faces on turn five is not the one they planned for on turn one. That is worth keeping. The change made is a swap of Mantine for Alomomola: Mantine's Water Absorb duplicated Tiffany's entire room concept four doors later, whereas Alomomola's Regenerator and Wish support is the natural partner for a manual-rain team that needs to survive the turn it spends setting weather. Overrepresented? Alomomola, Swanna, Wishiwashi, Golisopod and Primarina are each unique in the campaign; Lanturn's other owner is the route sailor Hudson in a Volt Absorb role. Bridget's room uses automatic Drizzle instead, so the gym has one manual-rain room and one automatic one by design. Levels: cap 84, offsets 2/2/2/2/2/3.
crack: Grass and Electric attacks cut through everything. Knock Wishiwashi under a quarter HP and it stops being a threat; push Golisopod to half and it removes itself. Replace the weather and Swanna loses both its Weather Ball power and its Hydration cure. Wide Guard blanks Liquid Voice Hyper Voice.

## E0461 TRAINER_BRIANNA class=gym
strategy: TRICK_ROOM
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Concept: room three - the deep, where the water stops moving. This is the gym's Trick Room room, and the deep has one law: nothing jumps the queue. Five slow Water bodies with zero Speed IVs, a sea cucumber whose knockout costs the attacker what it cost Brianna, and a Dazzling Bruxish whose glare makes every priority move aimed at Brianna's side fail - Fake Out, Grassy Glide, Sucker Punch, Aqua Jet, Extreme Speed and Prankster status included. First two useful turns: Bruxish and Slowking lead together and both know Trick Room, so stopping the room costs the player their whole turn instead of one attack. While Bruxish stands, Fake Out cannot flinch either setter; Bruxish's Focus Sash survives any single hit, and Slowking's Rindo Berry halves the Grass attack a Water gym expects, so one fast Grass attacker can no longer remove the only setter before the room's -7 priority resolves. Only one of them sets it - a second Trick Room in the same turn would cancel the first - and the other attacks: Slowking's Flamethrower is the room's answer to the Grass and Steel attackers that expect a Water gym to have nothing for them, and it lands on the turn that attacker spent hitting a berry. Turn two spends the room on damage; if the room was stopped, the surviving setter sets it then. Alternate deployment: Relicanth's Rock Head means Choice Band Head Smash costs it nothing, which under reversed order is the hardest single hit in the gym. Quagsire's Unaware ignores every stat boost the player has accumulated, so a Beast Boost, Shell Smash or Dragon Dance sweeper walks into a wall that does not care, and Ice Punch hits the Grass types that come for it. Reserves & disruption: Pyukumuku's Innards Out deals damage equal to the HP it had left to whatever knocks it out, so a fast attacker that takes it from full usually goes down with it; Counter and Mirror Coat return double the damage of a hit it survives, and Helping Hand powers Relicanth or Crawdaunt once the room lets them move first. Crawdaunt closes: Adaptability makes Crabhammer and Crunch hit twice as hard as a normal STAB would, Assault Vest covers its Special Defense, and Aqua Jet is the one move in the room that ignores the room. Slowking's Regenerator lets it leave and return to set the room again after five turns. Could this team be cooler? The playtest said it had to be. The whole plan rested on one Slowking, and a Life Orb Kartana beside an Incineroar's Fake Out removed it on turn one in every attempt; Trick Room never went up once, and six zero-Speed bodies were outsped and picked off by a Beast Boost snowball. Bruxish is the only Water body with a priority-blocking ability, so it turns the room's weak point into its lesson: the player's fast tricks do nothing here, and the plan that works is to spend real actions on the setters. Mental Herb gave way to the Rindo Berry because no Taunt was ever the threat; Toxapex's Wide Guard was never used and its Baneful Bunker set already belongs to the Seafloor Cavern grunt six encounters earlier, so its slot went to the second setter; Quagsire's Yawn, which only helped the player burn the room's turns by switching, became Ice Punch. Overrepresented? Bruxish's other owners are three Strong Jaw attackers and an Aqua Hideout grunt's Psychic Terrain lead; none sets Trick Room or carries a Sash, and no other Sootopolis room uses it. Pyukumuku and Quagsire appear in no other Sootopolis room; Crawdaunt's Assault Vest set differs from Shelly's Choice Band Close Combat one. Levels: cap 70, offsets 7/7/7/7/7/8.
crack: Spend a real turn on the setters. Knock Off ignores Bruxish's Sash and hits both Psychic setters super effectively, Spore or a non-priority Taunt stops a setter outright, and Dark, Ghost and Bug attacks hit both; a turn with both of your attacks on one setter, or one attack on each that the Sash and berry cannot absorb, keeps the room down. Priority does nothing while Bruxish is out, so knock it out first if your plan needs Fake Out, Sucker Punch or Grassy Glide. Once the room is up, bring your own Trick Room to reverse it, Protect and switch to burn its five turns, or lead with your slow Pokemon, which now move before Brianna's. Finish Pyukumuku with a weak attack you do not mind paying for, and never give it a big hit to Counter or Mirror Coat. Grass and Electric still answer most of the room - Relicanth and Quagsire take four times from Grass, Quagsire is immune to Electric, and Slowking survives one Grass hit to burn the attacker back; Fighting hits Relicanth and Crawdaunt, and after five turns the room ends while every member is still slow.

## E0462 TRAINER_CONNIE class=gym
strategy: SETUP,TAILWIND,ALLY_COMBO,REDIRECTION
mega_slots: NONE
tactic: ACTIVATE LUMINEON SURF GASTRODON
plan: Concept: room four - the redirection room, and the gym's cleverest single lesson. Every attack the room fears is pulled somewhere it cannot hurt: two Storm Drain bodies swallow Water, Seaking's Lightning Rod swallows Electric, and Magmar's Follow Me drags the Grass attack aimed at Gastrodon into a Fire type that shrugs it off. First two useful turns: the authored tactic fires Lumineon's Surf into the board, hitting both opponents while Gastrodon absorbs the friendly half and raises its own Special Attack by one stage; Gastrodon then attacks with a boosted Earth Power or recovers according to the resulting state. Turn two picks the best real target rather than repeating the mutual boost forever. Alternate deployment: against a Grass lead, Magmar is the replacement that changes the board. Follow Me pulls every single-target attack onto it, so a Grass hit meant for Gastrodon, which takes four times damage from Grass, lands on a Fire type that halves it; Follow Me is not a powder, so Grass types cannot ignore it the way they ignore Rage Powder. Flame Body can burn the physical Grass attacker that makes contact, Heat Wave hits both foes and a Grass/Steel attacker for four times damage, and Will-O-Wisp cripples the physical attacker Heat Wave cannot finish. Magmar's Pokedex says its heat waves ignite grass and trees, and Sootopolis is a volcano crater that filled with rain, so the one fire in the Water gym has a home in it. Follow Me also outranks Storm Drain and Lightning Rod while it lasts, so Magmar calls attention only when Grass is the threat, and it stays out of the Surf lane because Surf hits it for double. Seaking's Choice Band physical line and Octillery's Sniper special coverage are the mode to use when Storm Drain would get in the team's own way. Reserves & disruption: this is the one room in the gym where allied Storm Drain is an asset rather than a hazard, which is why Huntail's set carries no single-target Water attack at all - Shell Smash into Double-Edge, Crunch and Ice Fang keeps it entirely out of the redirection matrix, and the Double-Edge recoil is the price of staying off the Water lane. Could this team be cooler? The Storm Drain concept is one of the best ideas in the gym and stays exactly as it is, but a Grass pair swept the room in four turns: both Storm Drain bodies took double or quadruple damage from Grass and nothing on the team resisted it. The fix follows the room's own logic. Starmie, whose Hydro Pump and Thunderbolt were themselves being pulled into its allies' Storm Drain and Lightning Rod, gives its slot to the redirector that completes the set - Water, Electric and now Grass each have somewhere to go. Overrepresented? Seaking's Lightning Rod is unique to this room; Lumineon's other Storm Drain is a Mt. Pyre grunt's, and Gastrodon's three other owners are all Storm Drain sets away from Sootopolis; Starmie leaves the room and keeps five other owners; Magmar's only other owner is Axle's physical Vital Spirit set, and the Follow Me and Flame Body support idea last appeared on Dwayne's Magby at the start of the game, so this is its evolved echo.
crack: Grass attacks still hit both Storm Drain bodies hard, but while Magmar is calling them they land on Magmar instead: remove it first with Water, Ground or Rock attacks, beat Follow Me with Fake Out or Taunt, or aim a Water attack at the lead pair while Magmar is calling, because Follow Me outranks Storm Drain and sends it into the Fire type for double damage. Wide Guard blanks Surf entirely, which shuts the engine off in one move. Taunt stops Tailwind, Recover and Follow Me; exploit Seaking's Choice lock; Fire types ignore Will-O-Wisp and Heat Wave.

## E0465 TRAINER_TIFFANY class=gym
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Concept: room seven - the tide pool, built entirely on absorption. Three of the six are immune to Water attacks, so Vaporeon's spread Surf is a full-power attack on both opposing slots that heals its own partner instead of hurting it, and the one outsider absorbs the attack the rest of the pool is weakest to. First two useful turns: Vaporeon Surfs while a Water Absorb partner stands beside it, gaining a free quarter of HP for that ally; Seismitoad or Mantine attacks in the other slot. Turn two sets Wish only when a real recipient will still be alive at the end of the following turn. Sap Sipper makes it immune to Grass attacks and raises its Attack by one stage each time one is aimed at it, and Steel/Dragon typing resists Steel as well, so a Grass/Steel attacker is left with only its Fighting moves; Fire Punch hits Grass types for double and Grass/Steel types for four times, Heavy Slam is its Steel attack, and Breaking Swipe hits both foes and lowers their Attack, which blunts a physical Grass pair before it reaches Seismitoad, whose Ground half makes Grass four times as effective. Vaporeon's Surf does only half damage to Goodra's Dragon half, so the absorption pair can bring it in beside them at a small cost. Vaporeon's support also enables Barbaracle's White Herb Shell Smash, but Surf is genuinely unsafe beside Barbaracle, so the AI must switch lanes rather than blindly repeat the engine - the lead pair and the setup pair are two separate modes. Reserves & disruption: Feraligatr's Sheer Force Dragon Dance is the non-absorbing finisher; Tough Claws boosts every contact move Barbaracle has, and Sheer Force removes Life Orb recoil on Feraligatr's Liquidation, Ice Punch and Crunch. Could this team be cooler? The Water Absorb Surf engine is a clean, teachable idea and the right seventh room, but a Grass/Steel attacker hit Seismitoad and Whiscash for four times damage and its Beast Boost carried it through the rest. Whiscash was also the room's least distinctive member - an Assault Vest Oblivious set an Aqua Hideout grunt already carries - so its slot goes to a member that extends the absorption idea instead of breaking it: the tide pool drinks Water, and its one outsider drinks Grass. Overrepresented? Hisuian Goodra appears nowhere else in the campaign, and base Goodra's three owners are special ace-trainer sets; Whiscash leaves the room; Vaporeon's other owners include Hope in Victory Road with a Helping Hand support set; Seismitoad, Mantine, Barbaracle and Feraligatr each have other owners, none in the Sootopolis gym.
crack: Grass attacks still hit Seismitoad four times over and the other Water types twice, but not Hisuian Goodra, which is immune to them and grows stronger: remove it first with Fighting or Ground attacks, its only weaknesses, and lean on special attacks while Breaking Swipe is lowering your Attack. Electric answers Vaporeon and Mantine. Taunt stops Wish and Shell Smash. Attack Barbaracle or Feraligatr and the engine's own Surf becomes a liability the AI has to route around.

## E0466 TRAINER_BETHANY class=gym
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: 6
plan: Concept: room eight - the strike team. This is the gym's speed-and-priority room: everything here either moves first or hits before the player can react. First two useful turns: Palafin leads and uses Flip Turn or a hard switch only when a healthy receiver exists, because leaving the field transforms it into Hero Form - on its second entry it is a different, far larger Pokemon with a Jet Punch that outspeeds everything. Barraskewda attacks beside it with Propeller Tail, which cannot be pulled away by Follow Me, Rage Powder or Storm Drain. Turn two commits to whichever of the two transformations or boosts actually landed. Alternate deployment: Azumarill's Belly Drum is admitted only after a survival check - it costs half its HP for a maximised Attack that Huge Power then doubles again, making Aqua Jet a priority attack with no realistic counterplay except killing it first. Reserves & disruption: Greninja's Protean changes its type to match each move as it uses it, so it is never the type the player prepared for; Sniper Inteleon converts its critical hits into removals; Mega Kingler is the closer, with Crabhammer's high critical rate behind it and High Horsepower as the room's single answer to the Electric type that otherwise out-trades six Water bodies. Palafin's late placement must not strand an untransformed Hero with no reserve left to pivot into. Could this team be cooler? The Zero to Hero idea is the best single mechanic in the gym and stays as the room's spine, but the authored roster buried it: Dhelmise and Crawdaunt were slow bodies in a room about speed, and Mega Sharpedo made this the campaign's third owner of that exact stone after Archie and the Elite Four's Dark specialist. Rebuilding around Barraskewda, Greninja and Inteleon makes every slot serve the same idea, and Mega Kingler gives the room a Mega nobody else in the campaign fields. The memorable moment is the pivot itself - the player kills a modest dolphin and then meets Hero Form two turns later. Overrepresented? Mega Kingler, Palafin and Inteleon appear only here; Greninja's other owner is Felix's Mega version deep in Victory Road; Barraskewda's other owner is a Seafloor grunt with a Focus Sash; Azumarill's remaining owners are the route trainer Kara and nobody else, since Wally's Victory Road team is rebuilt to his canonical partners.
crack: Kill Palafin before it ever leaves the field and Hero Form never happens. Electric and Grass attacks answer the room, but keep the Electric type away from Mega Kingler's High Horsepower; priority of your own beats Jet Punch's users after Belly Drum. Fake Out and Intimidate both blunt the opening, and Inteleon and Greninja fold to any neutral hit.

## E0467 TRAINER_ANNIKA class=gym
strategy: SETUP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Concept: room nine - the still room. Annika is the gym's contrarian: her Golduck's Cloud Nine switches off every weather effect in the building, including her own colleagues' rain, and the rest of her team is built to win without any. First two useful turns: Golduck attacks or takes a Nasty Plot while Quaquaval opens with Aqua Step, which raises its own Speed on every use and stacks with Moxie's Attack boost after each knockout - a self-accelerating sweeper that needs no weather at all. Turn two uses the real boosts rather than adding a third. Alternate deployment: Empoleon's Competitive doubles its Special Attack whenever any stat of its is lowered, so an opposing Intimidate, Snarl or Icy Wind hands it a free Nasty Plot; Assault Vest bulk lets it stay in for that. Reserves & disruption: Milotic's Flame Orb self-burn activates Marvel Scale for a 50% Defence boost at the cost of residual damage, and Hisuian Samurott's Sharpness sharply boosts its slicing moves while Ceaseless Edge lays Spikes on every hit; its Choice Band Drill Run is the room's answer to the Electric type that would otherwise sweep it, and Sucker Punch keeps the Dark coverage Knock Off used to add. Basculegion is the Adaptability special closer. Note that Aqua Step is a dance, so an opposing Dancer copies it. Could this team be cooler? Yes, and it needed the change more than any other room except Brianna's. Pyukumuku's Counter-and-Toxic opening was pure passivity in a gym that is supposed to be eleven consecutive benchmarks, and the block's own prose flagged it for anti-passivity testing. Replacing it with Basculegion gives the room a real sixth threat, a Water/Ghost typing nothing else in the gym has, and an immunity to the Fighting and Normal attacks the player brings for Empoleon and Milotic. What remains is the room's genuinely distinctive idea - three different self-boosting mechanisms (Aqua Step, Moxie, Competitive) that all reward the player for attacking, so patience is punished and impatience is punished differently. Overrepresented? Quaquaval, Empoleon, Hisuian Samurott and Basculegion are unique in the campaign; Milotic's other owner is Champion Wallace's Mega; Golduck's Cloud Nine echoes the route sailor Hudson deliberately, as the player-side lesson resurfacing as an opponent.
crack: Do not lower Empoleon's stats. Electric and Grass attacks answer most of the room, but a Band-locked Samurott's Drill Run punishes the Electric type - lure it into Ceaseless Edge first or remove it; Dark and Ghost hit Basculegion. Haze erases Aqua Step and Moxie together, Taunt stops Nasty Plot, and Milotic's burn is doing steady damage to itself all fight.

## E0468 TRAINER_DAPHNE class=gym
strategy: SNOW
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Concept: room ten - the freeze. The last room before Juan is the one that changes the weather itself: Lapras lays down snow by hand, which raises every Ice type's Defence by half, and the room's Ice Body members then heal from the same storm every turn. First two useful turns: Lapras opens with Snowscape when the team can bank the Defence boost and the passive healing, or with Freeze-Dry, which is the room's signature - an Ice attack that is super effective against Water, so this room beats the rest of its own gym. Walrein attacks beside it with Thick Fat cutting incoming Fire and Ice damage in half. Turn two uses the real weather state and picks between Blizzard's now-perfect accuracy and single-target damage. Alternate deployment: Cryogonal's Levitate makes it immune to Ground attacks, and its Icy Wind and Rapid Spin support Samurott's physical line. Reserves & disruption: snow makes Blizzard never miss, so Walrein's Choice Specs lock is far less dangerous than it looks once the weather is up; Rotom-Wash supplies the Electric coverage the room otherwise lacks and Levitate keeps it out of Ground range; Fur Coat halves physical damage against Dewgong. Could this team be cooler? It is now the room the gym was missing. The authored version had no engine at all - four unrelated Water types plus a Tapu Fini that duplicated Champion Wallace's own legend, which is exactly the kind of collision that makes a later fight feel less special. Rebuilding Daphne as the snow room gives Sootopolis its eleventh distinct strategy, hands Freeze-Dry to the one trainer for whom being a Water gym's worst matchup is the joke, and lets Walrein's Blizzard finally be accurate somewhere. Cryogonal is the rare, genuinely strange body the room deserves: a floating ice crystal with enormous Special Defence and no Ground weakness. Overrepresented? Cryogonal, Walrein and Dewgong appear only here in the gym; Lapras's other owners are the route trainer Everett's Perish Song set and Micah's Mega far into the post-game; Rotom-Wash recurs with Keira after the League. Tapu Fini is returned to Champion Wallace alone. Levels: cap 84, offsets 2/2/2/2/2/3.
crack: Replace the weather and the Defence boost, the healing and Blizzard's accuracy all go at once. Fire, Fighting, Rock and Steel attacks cover the Ice core; Samurott and Rotom-Wash are the only members that are not weak to Fighting. Taunt stops Snowscape and Rapid Spin, and Walrein is locked into whatever it picked.

## E0469 TRAINER_JUAN_1 class=leader
strategy: RAIN,SETUP
mega_slots: 6
ai: Double Ace Pokemon
plan: Concept: the eleventh door - Juan takes the rain his gym has been teaching and uses it for attrition rather than burst, then ends the fight with a Mega. Everything the ten rooms showed the player in isolation arrives here at once, and the two answers a player brings to a Water gym - thunder and ice - each meet a member chosen to stop them. First two useful turns: Politoed's Drizzle is live on entry with a Damp Rock behind it, and Empoleon leads beside it as the door's answer to ice. Water/Steel takes Freeze-Dry at neutral and Ice Beam or Blizzard at a quarter, resists Dragon, is immune to Sludge Bomb, and its Life Orb Flash Cannon removes a Choice Specs Kyurem in one hit; Protect is for the turn a Fake Out and a Ground attack are both aimed at it, which also wastes the Fake Out for good, and Icy Wind lowers both foes' Speed so Empoleon and Kingdra move first afterwards. Competitive turns an opposing Intimidate into +2 Special Attack. Politoed spends its turn on Ice Beam into the Grass or Dragon partner, Encore on a support move the player has just repeated (Rage Powder, Protect, Follow Me), or spread Muddy Water; the lead pair must trade damage from turn one, because Juan's failure mode is passivity. Alternate deployment: Choice Scarf Landorus-Therian is the answer to thunder and comes off the bench, never the lead, because a turn-one Fake Out beside any Ice attack removes it before it acts. Ground typing makes it immune to Electric, Intimidate lands on entry, and the Scarf moves it before the Electric/Dragon legends without a turn of speed control: Stomping Tantrum hits an Electric/Dragon or Electric/Fighting body for double without catching a partner in a quake, Superpower and Rock Slide hit an Ice/Dragon attacker for double, and U-turn carries the Intimidate back out to use again. In the Unova myth Landorus is the one that reins in Thundurus and Tornadus; Juan, who keeps the rain, keeps the legend that grounds the thunder inside it. Manaphy is the answer to sleep: Hydration cures its status at the end of every rain turn, so a Spore or Sleep Powder aimed at it costs at most the turn it lands, and Tail Glow (+3 Special Attack) is the payoff when the player's best move into it is a powder; Psychic hits Grass/Poison sleep users for double, Energy Ball hits a Storm Drain Gastrodon or any Water/Ground body four times over, and Scald is the rain-boosted STAB. Reserves & disruption: Choice Specs Swift Swim Kingdra is the burst reserve, doubling its Speed in rain it did not have to set - Draco Meteor for Dragons, Hurricane, which never misses in rain, for the Grass types that resist Water and for Fighting types, Ice Beam for Ground and Flying. Mega Gyarados is the closer, with Intimidate deliberately spent before transformation: Mold Breaker means Waterfall damages a Storm Drain or Water Absorb body instead of feeding it, Taunt shuts off a Spore or Rage Powder user before it can put the closer to sleep, and Dragon Dance turns one free turn into a sweep. Counterplay & audit: the pair AI picks replacements by matchup rather than planning a pivot, so Landorus usually arrives on a replacement into an Electric attacker; Juan has no weather answer of his own beyond sending Politoed back in. Could this team be cooler? The previous version folded to one Choice Specs Kyurem: Freeze-Dry was super effective on all six members, a turn-one Fake Out plus Freeze-Dry deleted the lead Landorus before it acted in eight of nine benchmark attempts, and Altaria's Cloud Nine switched off Juan's own Swift Swim and Hydration whenever it stood beside them, which let Spore put Kingdra and Gyarados to sleep for the turns that decided the fight. Altaria leaves; Empoleon takes the lead beside Politoed, Landorus moves to the bench where its Electric immunity still answers the thunder, and every reserve gains a move aimed at the counter that beat it - Hurricane and Psychic for the sleep core, Taunt for the Spore user, Flash Cannon for the ice. Overrepresented? Landorus-Therian and Manaphy are unique to this fight. Empoleon's other owners are Shelly at the Weather Institute and Annika's ninth room, both Choice-free attackers built around Hydro Pump and Ice Beam; Juan's leads with Icy Wind, Protect and a Life Orb Flash Cannon, the leader's version of the lesson that room taught. Politoed's Drizzle is shared with Darrin, an Aqua Hideout grunt and Shelly in Seafloor Cavern; Kingdra has four other owners and Mega Gyarados one (Darrin), all earlier in the game, and none of those Kingdra carries Hurricane. Altaria leaves this fight, so Wally's Tailwind Altaria seven fights later no longer repeats the species.
crack: Juan has no Electric resistance on the field until Landorus arrives - an Electric attacker hits both Politoed and Empoleon for double on turn one. Empoleon takes Ground and Fighting for double and has no recovery: bait its Protect, then hit it with Earth Power. Freeze-Dry is still super effective on five members, four times over on Landorus and Kingdra, so an Ice attacker that keeps away from Empoleon stays dangerous. Landorus holds a Choice Scarf: it has no Protect and is locked after its first move - switch a Flying type or Levitate user into the Ground attack. Take the weather and keep taking it: sun halves every Water attack and switches off Swift Swim and Hydration, so Kingdra slows and Manaphy can be slept again. Grass attacks hit Politoed, Manaphy and Mega Gyarados for double, and a Storm Drain partner draws Juan's single-target Water attacks; only Mega Gyarados's Mold Breaker still damages it. Sleep still lands on everyone but Manaphy in rain - put Kingdra or Gyarados to sleep before Taunt arrives. Taunt stops Encore, Tail Glow and Dragon Dance; Haze erases both boosts, and priority or a Fairy attack finishes Gyarados after it dances.

## E0475 TRAINER_EVERETT class=regular
strategy: PERISH_TRAP
mega_slots: NONE
plan: Concept: the campaign's perish-trap prototype - Wobbuffet's Shadow Tag forbids the player from switching, Lapras starts a three-turn countdown, and both sides watch the clock. Turn two plays the countdown honestly - the trapper must leave or deliberately trade before it reaches zero, and switching the trapper releases the opponents early. Alternate deployment: Beheeyem and Musharna are the slower control fallback when the trap is answered - Analytic adds 30% to Beheeyem's damage whenever it moves last, which a Trick Room makes reliable. Reserves & disruption: Life Dew heals both allies, Safeguard blocks the status a trapped player reaches for, and Forewarn tells Musharna the strongest move on the opposing side. Wobbuffet is deliberately given no Protect - the script must not be made easy. Could this team be cooler? The perish trap is the rarest strategy in the campaign and appears exactly once, which is the right frequency; a second owner would make it a gimmick rather than an event. The block carried one legality error - Beheeyem cannot learn Helping Hand - so it becomes Energy Ball, which also gives the control half a real answer to the Ground and Water types that otherwise wall it. The honest limitation stays recorded: countdown ordering, simultaneous faints and escape sequencing are native acceptance gates, not assumptions. Overrepresented? Wobbuffet, Beheeyem and Musharna's Forewarn set are unique; Lapras's other owners are Daphne's gym ice room and Micah's post-game Mega. Levels: cap 90, offsets 0/1/1/1.
crack: Ghost types ignore Shadow Tag entirely, and so do Shed Shell and U-turn. Soundproof blocks Perish Song. Kill Wobbuffet with a spread move so Counter and Mirror Coat cannot answer, or simply out-damage the clock - three turns is not long, and Lapras dies to Electric and Grass attacks.

## E0476 TRAINER_WALLY_VR_1 class=rival
strategy: TAILWIND,MEGA_REVEAL
mega_slots: 2
plan: Concept: the rival arc, part one, and the last rival fight before the League. These are the partners Wally has raised since Petalburg, built this time to beat the Fire-and-Steel team that is the obvious way through a Psychic/Fairy/Grass core. First two useful turns: Ludicolo and Gallade lead, and MEGA_REVEAL evolves Gallade at the start of turn one. Mega Gallade's ability is Inner Focus, not Sharpness, and it applies before anyone moves: an opposing Fake Out cannot flinch it, and any Intimidate that switches in later cannot lower its Attack. A lead Intimidate lands before the turn-one Mega, so Gallade may open at -1. Ludicolo uses Fake Out on the foe whose attack matters most that turn, usually the spread Fire user or whichever foe threatens Gallade. Meanwhile Gallade's Sacred Sword ignores Defense boosts and hits Fire, Steel, Dark and Rock super effectively. On turn two Ludicolo's Muddy Water hits both foes, and Water is super effective on Fire, Rock and Ground, so a Fire pair takes it on both sides at once. Assault Vest and Water typing let Ludicolo absorb Heat Wave, and Own Tempo ignores Intimidate. Ice Beam covers Ground, Dragon and Flying; Giga Drain covers Water, Rock and Ground and heals Ludicolo. Knock Off takes the item from a Ghost or Psychic target, and Psycho Cut is Gallade's STAB answer to Fighting and Poison. Alternate deployment: Altaria resists Fire, Water, Grass and Electric; it sets Tailwind, uses Roost to stay healthy, Dragon Pulse on Dragons and Flamethrower on Steel and Grass. Magnezone's Magnet Pull traps Steel types, including a Fire/Steel Mega Heatran, so they cannot switch away from Sacred Sword, Muddy Water or Magnezone's own Body Press. Body Press is calculated from Magnezone's Defense and hits Steel, Rock, Dark, Ice and Normal super effectively. Air Balloon is the Mauville Magneton's balloon: it keeps Magnezone off the ground until the first hit pops it. Reserves & disruption: when Gardevoir enters, Trace copies an ability from the opposing side; if it copies Heatran's Flash Fire, Gardevoir becomes immune to Fire. Moonblast covers Dragon, Dark and Fighting; Mystical Fire covers Steel, Grass and Bug and lowers the target's Special Attack; Focus Blast is Gardevoir's answer to Fire/Steel and Rock/Dark. Eviolite Roselia lands Sleep Powder, and Natural Cure clears its own status when it switches out. Never fire Mystical Fire or Flamethrower into Flash Fire, never aim Sleep Powder at a Grass type, and do not keep Magnezone in to trap a Steel type the side cannot damage. Could this team be cooler? Yes. The previous version answered its own counter with nothing. Delcatty spent the fight on Helping Hand and Heal Bell. Gardevoir's Psychic hit almost nothing on a Steel and Dark team. The Mega sat in the last slot behind Ace Pokemon and arrived only after spread Fire had removed the Fire-weak Grass and Steel members, so a Fire-and-Steel team won on attempt one with four standing. Now the Mega leads and ignores the Fake Out a Fire lead relies on. The Fake Out comes from a Water type that punishes the Fire lead with a spread move, and the trapper keeps a Fire/Steel attacker on the field for Gallade's Sacred Sword. The new member is canon-adjacent: Lotad shares the Route 102 grass where Wally caught Ralts, Ludicolo is fished from that same pond, and Lotad swims the river at Verdanturf, Wally's new home. Overrepresented? Ludicolo's most recent owner is Shelly at Seafloor Cavern, twenty-two encounters earlier, and none of its five other trainers uses Assault Vest or Muddy Water. Juan's Altaria is a Cloud Nine attacker; Wally's is a Tailwind support. Hannah's Mega Gallade is a Leaf Blade attacker, and Roselia belongs only to Wally and Daisy. In the post-League rematch Gallade gives the Mega to Altaria, so the two fights mirror each other.
crack: On turn one, Protect whichever foe Sacred Sword is likely to hit. Alternatively, lead a Ghost, Flying or Fairy attacker faster than Mega Gallade's base 110 Speed; Gallade has only 68 base HP and the whole plan runs through it. Fake Out still works on Ludicolo, and a lead Intimidate lowers Gallade before it evolves. Ludicolo is weak to Flying, Poison and Bug, and Assault Vest means it cannot Protect. Wide Guard blocks Muddy Water, and Water Absorb, Storm Drain and Dry Skin absorb it. Fire still hits Magnezone and Roselia super effectively. Any hit pops Magnezone's Air Balloon, after which Ground does four times damage; Fighting is also super effective. Taunt stops Tailwind and Roost, and Ice, Rock, Dragon and Fairy attacks hit Altaria super effectively. Steel and Poison attacks answer Gardevoir, and Focus Blast misses 30% of the time. Grass types, Overcoat and Safety Goggles ignore Sleep Powder.

## E0480 TRAINER_QUINCY class=ace
strategy: REDIRECTION,TAILWIND

plan: Concept: the cleverest single idea in Victory Road - a team built entirely around turning off the worst abilities in the game. Slaking has Truant and can only attack every other turn; Weezing's Neutralizing Gas suppresses every ability on the field while it is alive, Truant included, so a Choice Scarf Slaking with 160 base Attack simply attacks every turn instead. The authored SUPPRESS tactic is what tells the AI to keep Weezing alive for exactly that reason. Turn two protects the suppressor - the moment Weezing dies, Slaking loses half its turns. Reserves & disruption: Terrakion's Quick Guard blocks the priority aimed at Weezing. The ace is Archeops, the gas's second beneficiary: its Defeatist halves its Attack and Special Attack once it drops below half HP, and under Neutralizing Gas that drawback simply does not exist, so a 140-Attack Rock/Flying bird hits at full power however hurt it is. Its Sitrus Berry is the backup for when the gas is gone - it pulls Archeops back above the Defeatist line once. Rock Slide and Dual Wingbeat avoid the Earthquake that would hit Weezing, which has Neutralizing Gas rather than Levitate. Every slot serves one legible idea: the player beats it by killing a Weezing, and doing so visibly halves Slaking and cripples Archeops at the same time.
crack: Kill Weezing and the fight halves. Psychic and Ground attacks answer it; Fighting answers Slaking; Fire answers Durant and Butterfree. Do not let Durant touch your sweeper with Entrainment. Quick Guard only blocks priority, so remove the suppressor with an ordinary attack. Once the gas is gone, chip Archeops below half and it stops hitting hard; Rock, Steel, Electric, Ice and Water answer it, and Wide Guard blanks its Rock Slide.
